Grand Theft Auto 6 Is Almost Out. Here’s How to Make Room on Your Console

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1118 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the wait is almost over.
  • Industry observers note that rockstar Games revealed that GTA 6 is 212 GB, which will take up about half of my Xbox Series S’s storage space.
  • Sources indicate that if you’re like me and are excited to play GTA 6 but don’t have much storage space, you have two options: delete games or upgrade your console’s hard drive.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the wait is almost over. Grand Theft Auto 6 hits shelves tomorrow, Nov. 19, and if you preordered the game, you can preload it on your PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S now. Preloading ensures you can swiftly boot the game up when it’s released.

Industry observers note that rockstar Games revealed that GTA 6 is 212 GB, which will take up about half of my Xbox Series S’s storage space. The firm announced that GTA 6 is available to stream via Xbox Cloud Gaming without downloading it to your console. However, cloud streaming GTA 6 might affect the game’s performance and relies heavily on a strong internet connection. To avoid those problems, I plan on downloading the game.

Sources indicate that if you’re like me and are excited to play GTA 6 but don’t have much storage space, you have two options: delete games or upgrade your console’s hard drive. Here’s what you should know about both options.

Sources indicate that the simplest and cheapest way to free up space on your console for Grand Theft Auto 6 is to delete files and other games, which is what I’ll be doing. Uninstalling games is a good choice for folks who initiative on spending a lot of time with GTA 6 and don’t intend to juggle different games. Rob Nelson, who oversees Rockstar North with Aaron Garbut, told The Upcoming York Times that he had an 80-hour playthrough of the game in February, so you can easily stay immersed in Grand Theft Auto’s state of Leonida.

It has been revealed that you may not need to delete much – uninstalling a game like Call of Duty alone could free up nearly 315 GB, giving you enough digital storage for GTA 6. Since deleting files is almost instantaneous, you can promptly reclaim hard drive space. Because you don’t need to buy additional storage, you’ll also save a lot of money – storage prices are through the roof at the moment.

Ultimately, deleting games is a great option if you don’t want to spend any additional money or you don’t mind redownloading games later.

Industry observers note that if you plan on hopping between GTA 6 and other games, or you don’t want to delete many of your downloaded titles, you can upgrade your console’s storage. Buying storage is more expensive than deleting files from your console, but benefit from being able to seamlessly hop between Grand Theft Auto 6 and Call of Duty or Madden.

According to recent reports, you can use internal or external storage for your console, but you might have to move files between your internal and external storage to launch games. An internal hard drive lets you seamlessly play games. Xbox consoles rely on proprietary expansion cards from Seagate or SanDisk that plug into your console for additional storage. The PlayStation 5 uses M.2 solid-state drives, which are installed alongside the PS5’s built-in storage, and CNET’s David Carnoy recommends the Lexar NM 790 as a fast SSD with a straightforward installation process.

Recent findings suggest that there shouldn’t be any performance, quality or load-time differences between running games from installed storage expansion devices versus your console’s internal storage. Both expansion cards and SSDs can be expensive, especially when compared with deleting games.

You could also use an external hard drive to expand your storage, which can be cheaper than buying expansion cards and internal SSD upgrades – you may even have a compatible USB external drive sitting around that you can use. However, there are caveats around what games can and can’t be played directly from external HDDs.

For Xbox consoles, some older Xbox, Xbox 360 and Xbox One titles can be stored and played from external HDDs. But games optimized for Series X/S consoles can only be stored on HDDs and must be moved back to your internal drive to play. Similarly, the PlayStation 5 only lets you store PS5 games on external HDDs, while you can store and run PS4 games from external drives.

Therefore, using an external HDD requires playing digital musical chairs, moving current-gen games back and forth between your external hard drive and internal console storage in order to play them. The LaCie Rugged SSD4 earned a CNET Editors’ Choice Award and could be a good option. If its price tag scares you, the Western Digital P10 offers more storage at a more economical price point.

Rockstar unveiled that GTA 6 will be available to stream on the Xbox consoles – no download required – via Xbox Cloud Gaming, with some quality and time limitations. You’ll need to purchase either an Xbox Game Pass proposal or Cloud Gaming hours. Folks who don’t want to delete games or upgrade their console storage can stream GTA 6, but you’ll need an Xbox One or Series X/S console, won’t get the highest visual quality and will have to pay for more playtime hours if they run out. Streaming GTA 6 could help budget-conscious gamers who don’t want to upgrade from Xbox One consoles or who don’t have the allotted storage space on their devices.

Normally, you can stream many games on PCs, mobile devices and TVs or streaming devices using Xbox Cloud Gaming or Game Pass, but Grand Theft Auto 6 is limited to the Xbox One, Series S and Series X. Additionally, GTA 6 streaming quality is capped at Series S graphical settings. So if you have a Series X, consider deleting games or upgrading your storage to run the game locally with better graphics.

While you’ll need to install the full game on your console first, remote play for Xbox and PlayStation consoles lets you stream GTA 6 to other devices, like your phone, tablet, streaming device or TV.

It has been revealed that if you’re willing to pay a little more for the convenience of having multiple games ready to play at a moment’s notice, Xbox expansion cards or an internal SSD for a PS5 are your best options. If you want a cheaper option and don’t mind moving game files around, an external hard drive could be for you. If you have Xbox Game Pass or Xbox Cloud Gaming, you could stream the game to your console without needing more storage space. However, the cheapest option is to delete games from your internal storage and redownload them later, which can be time-consuming.

You only have a few days left until Rockstar releases GTA 6, so you’d better prepare your digital storage now, or you might not be immediately able to play. I initiative on deleting old games to make room on my console. You won’t catch me slipping on Nov. 19.

Industry News: Disney Imagineers Have Built AI-Powered ‘Star Wars’ Alien Audio-Animatronics With AWS

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (844 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, disney is celebrating 75 years of its Imagineers, who have been amusing and delighting guests with audio-animatronic characters since talking parrots debuted in the Enchanted Tiki Room at Disneyland.
  • In partnership with Amazon Web Services, AI has helped Walt Disney Imagineering create three latest Anzellan animatronics that will live bring a Disney theme park retail space to life, presumably in Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge.
  • Anzellans are a race of tiny humanoid creatures that repair droids and starships in the Star Wars universe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, disney is celebrating 75 years of its Imagineers, who have been amusing and delighting guests with audio-animatronic characters since talking parrots debuted in the Enchanted Tiki Room at Disneyland. But today, latest robotic characters are being powered up with artificial intelligence.

In partnership with Amazon Web Services, AI has helped Walt Disney Imagineering create three latest Anzellan animatronics that will live bring a Disney theme park retail space to life, presumably in Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge.

Anzellans are a race of tiny humanoid creatures that repair droids and starships in the Star Wars universe. They include Babu Frik in Star Wars: Episode IX — The Rise of Skywalker and the droidsmiths introduced in season 3 of The Mandalorian. The droidsmiths take on larger roles in The Mandalorian and Grogu, helping Baby Yoda rescue Din Djarin from the Hutts.

The upcoming Anzellan animatronics built by Disney Imagineers use AWS cloud and AI capabilities in order to “understand the scene around them,” Kyle Laughlin, SVP of Walt Disney Imagineering R&D and Technology and Engineering, tells me.

“If you imagine walking into an experiential retail store, you now will be greeted not by a pre-scripted animation or interaction, but a totally personalized experience where each of these Anzellans [has] their own personalities,” Laughlin claims, adding that they’ll be attuned to “how many people are in the room, the ages of people, the general size and type of guest.”.

Recent findings suggest that the animatronic aliens will be able to interact with guests, right down to commenting on people who are wearing a birthday button or even a certain Star Wars T-shirt. Speaking with these animatronics will give guests the same experience they would have when meeting a character walking around the park, Laughlin adds. They also play off each other and react to what each other are doing, with no one controlling them behind the scenes.

Recent findings suggest that the three audio-animatronic prototypes, which will make their first appearance during AWS re:Invent in Las Vegas on Nov. 30 before moving into one of the Disney Parks, are named Vilo Vele, Kado Bre’a and Jibu Bre’a.

They’re original characters created just for this project in partnership with Lucasfilm and the filmmakers, and they all have their own personalities devised by the Imagineers. Vilo is the boss, Kado is the droidsmith mechanic who wants to be the center of attention and Jibu, though Kado’s twin, is the shy one. The animatronics speak a mix of English (or Galactic Basic in-universe) and Anzellan, as they do in the Star Wars movies and TV series, and have hundreds of thousands of prerecorded lines of dialogue to draw from when talking to guests and each other.

Samira Panah Bakhtiar, AWS general manager of Telco, Media & Entertainment, Games, Advertising and Sports, tells me this is “one of the most delightful examples” of physical AI.

“When you talk about physical AI, it’s AI that perceives, it reasons and it acts in the real world,” she says. “It’s not just AI on a screen.”.

Bakhtiar states Disney was able to use both AWS cloud computing and AI tools to “get from idea to implementation several magnitudes faster than they would have otherwise,” with Laughlin specifying it took “mere months.”.

Sources indicate that imagineers used an AWS coding agent called Kiro that built their creative briefs into software, which was then reviewed by humans. Imagineers also used the Amazon Bedrock fully managed AI service, which allows them to choose between all the biggest AI models, including those from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta.

“We’re providing Amazon Bedrock to the Imagineering team to be able to leverage the right models that they need at the right time to be able to really enhance those character experiences,” Bakhtiar tells me. “From multimodal models that focus on voice to world models, to large language models. The point is that they are able to get the right tool at the right time and then do so in a way that’s secure, resilient, performant and globally available.”.

Bakhtiar claims AWS is continuing to work with Disney, though the next project is under wraps.

In a recent development, “The future of entertainment is going to be highly personalized,” she says. “It’s going to be multidimensional, and it’s going to be more interactive than ever. And I think this is an incredible example of that coming to life.”.

Disney had previously teamed up with Nvidia on robotics and AI to bring a robot version of fan-favorite Frozen character Olaf to life so he can wander around Disneyland Paris and Hong Kong Disneyland, and is also now exploring robots paired with AI that could guide guests throughout Disneyland parking lots.

“You can imagine an entire franchise of characters working and interacting with one another,” indicates Laughlin. “We’ve done a number of things in the Star Wars universe. We’re just getting started in Frozen, and we have a wealth of IP that we can mine to bring those characters to our guests as fast as possible.”.

10 stocks we like better than Celsius Holdings ›.

Choosing between growth and stability often defines an investment strategy. You might consider whether the rapid expansion of Celsius (CELH +4.62%) or the enduring legacy of Hershey (HSY +0.21%) is the better buy.

It has been revealed that celsius represents the high-growth side of the beverage market, focusing on functional energy drinks that appeal to health-conscious consumers. Hershey remains a cornerstone of the confectionery world, offering massive scale and predictable returns through its dominant position in chocolate and snacks.

Recent findings suggest that celsius focuses on the functional beverage market, selling energy drinks designed to boost metabolism and provide sustained energy. It reaches consumers through major retailers and e-commerce platforms like Amazon (AMZN +1.55%), while competing among beverage stocks for shelf space. A critical component of its strategy is a distribution agreement with Pepsi, which provides the necessary infrastructure to scale quickly. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as Pepsi accounted for roughly 43.2% of revenue recently.

Recent findings suggest that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $3.2 billion. This figure represents revenue growth of approximately 49.1% compared to the prior twelve-month period. During the same window, the firm reported net income of nearly $230.2 million, demonstrating its ability to maintain profitability as it scales its footprint across North America and international markets.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.2x. This ratio compares total debt to shareholder equity, indicating how much the firm relies on borrowing to fund its operations. The current ratio, which measures the ability to cover short-term liabilities with current assets, is roughly 1.7x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was nearly $72.1 million. Free cash flow represents the cash a company generates after accounting for cash outflows to support operations and maintain its capital assets.

Industry observers note that hershey operates as a global leader in the confectionery and snacking industry, producing well-known brands ranging from chocolate bars to protein snacks. The company sells its products through wholesale distributors and major retail chains, with McLane Company, Inc. serving as its largest customer, accounting for approximately 27% of net sales. This customer concentration adds a layer of risk to the business, though Hershey offsets this with a presence in over 65 countries. Its strategy emphasizes brand loyalty and consistent product innovation to maintain its market-leading position.

In a recent development, in the 12 months ended Sept. 27, 2026, revenue reached close to $12.3 billion. This reflects revenue growth of approximately 6.7% over the previous year, showing steady progress in a mature market. The company reported net income of nearly $1.8 billion during this period, highlighting the strong cash-generating power of its established brand portfolio.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 1.2x. The current ratio is approximately 1.2x, suggesting the manufacturer maintains sufficient liquidity to meet its immediate financial obligations. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was close to $1.8 billion. This robust cash generation allows the company to support its operations and return value to shareholders through various capital allocation strategies.

Celsius faces significant revenue concentration with Pepsi, creating a high level of dependency on a single partner for distribution. The company also faces intense competition from global brands like Monster Beverage (MNST +1.14%) and Coca-Cola (KO -0.09%). Operational risks include a reliance on third-party co-packers and potential supply chain disruptions for aluminum cans and specific ingredients. Furthermore, the integration of fresh brands like Alani Nu could lead to operational challenges or cannibalize its existing product lines.

Recent findings suggest that hershey faces significant commodity price volatility, especially in cocoa and sugar, which can affect its gross margin. The company must also manage the risk of sales volume declines if price increases intended to offset rising input costs lead to consumer pushback. Competition from global giants like Nestlé (NSRGF -4.46%) remains a constant pressure, requiring continuous marketing and innovation. Additionally, Hershey faces complexities in international operations and potential cybersecurity threats that could disrupt its global supply chain.

Celsius trades at a slightly higher earnings multiple than Hershey, though its lower price-to-sales ratio might appeal to those prioritizing rapid revenue expansion.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

The Forward P/E provides a look at the stock price relative to future earnings estimates, while the P/S ratio measures the market value against sales over the past twelve months.

While Celsius certainly offers the more exciting growth profile versus steady-Eddie Hershey, its organic sales growth likely lies closer to the high single digits as of its most recent quarter. Celsius's skyrocketing revenue in 2026 primarily came from adding Alani Nu to its operations via its $1.8 billion acquisition of the up-and-coming energy drink maker, rather than true organic sales growth.

That mentioned, Alani Nu rapidly surpassed the organization's namesake Celsius brand as its best-selling drink -- and its growth isn't slowing yet. Alani Nu grew revenue by 24% (product sold to distributors) and saw retail sales rise 58% (product sold at c-stores, or grocery stores, for example), highlighting the brand's growing popularity. On top of Alani Nu's success, Celsius grew international revenue by 78%, and these foreign sales account for just 5% of the company's total revenue, leaving a potentially decades-long growth runway ahead.

With a portfolio of Alani Nu, Celsius, Rockstar, and international sales, Celsius should provide reasonable growth upside over the foreseeable future -- just don't expect 2026's growth rates to repeat, barring another major acquisition.

Industry observers note that hershey, meanwhile, is a stalwart chocolatier and snacking behemoth paying a well-funded and growing dividend that yields 3.3%. The company's days of consistent double-digit sales growth are behind it, but management expects adjusted EPS to rise by roughly 7% annually over the long term. Leaning on its strategy as a serial acquirer, I fully expect Hershey to meet this goal as it builds out its steadily growing salty snacks portfolio (primarily popcorn and pretzels). GLP-1 medications certainly pose a threat to Hershey's business, but I believe the peptide may, counterintuitively, be a benefit to the company, as miniaturization and smaller packaging could boost margins.

According to recent reports, ultimately, I'm not in a rush to buy more shares of either stock, though I do own both. However, I would lean toward buying Celsius in 2027, given its stronger growth potential and similar valuation to Hershey. Investors seeking stability and passive income may be better off buying Hershey, though, so it comes down to any individual investor's goals and risk appetite.

Industry News: Today, Voyager 1 Becomes the First Spacecraft a Full Light-Day From Home

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1082 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • NASA’s Voyager 1 left Earth on Sept.
  • Industry observers note that at 5:16:07 a.m.
  • Industry observers note that NASA puts the journey at 49 years, two months and 11 days, counting from Voyager 1’s launch in September 1977.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA’s Voyager 1 left Earth on Sept. 5, 1977, carrying a camera, a set of science instruments and a gold-plated record of sounds and images from home. Forty-nine years later, it’s about to reach a distance no spacecraft has reached before: one light-day, or roughly 16.1 billion miles, from Earth. At that range, light needs a full 24 hours to make the trip between Earth and the probe.

Industry observers note that at 5:16:07 a.m. ET today on Wednesday, November 18, Voyager 1 became the first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth, about 16.1 billion miles away. From that point on, a radio signal between the spacecraft and NASA’s Deep Space Network takes more than a day to arrive in either direction.

Industry observers note that NASA puts the journey at 49 years, two months and 11 days, counting from Voyager 1’s launch in September 1977. The probe still sends data home, though at a rate slower than dial-up, and NASA looks a live discussion with the Voyager team on Thursday to mark the occasion.

It’s quite an accomplishment for a spacecraft built in the mid-1970s. One light-day is the distance that light travels in a single day at the speed of light, which is approximately 186,282 miles per second. That translates to 25.9 billion kilometers or about 16.1 billion miles in a single day. At an average human walking speed of 3 mph, it would take a human 612,015 years to walk that distance.

Fortunately, Voyager 1 has been traveling a bit faster than humans can walk. It currently zips along the cosmos at a steady 37,763 mph, a speed it achieved in 1980 after a gravity-assisted Saturn flyby. It has been flying at that speed ever since.

The milestone comes 14 years after its previous one, when Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause, the point where the sun’s heliosphere ends, and entered interstellar space. It’s also 28 years after passing Pioneer 10 to become the human-made object that has traveled the farthest into space.

It has been revealed that NASA is marking the milestone with a global Shine Bright for Voyager’s Light-Day event on Tuesday evening. Just after sunset, the agency wants people to head outside and point their smartphone or tablet lights skyward, sparking a planet-wide wave of light as Earth rotates, much like fans doing the wave at a stadium.

NASA also made a website for the occasion. The website is simple. It flashes Voyager’s VGR call sign in Morse code. If you want to try it, click the link, hit begin, and then point your phone or tablet screen at the sky. The website does all the work for you.

NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory will follow up on Thursday at noon ET with a moderated discussion on the milestone, featuring status updates on both Voyager probes and a live Q&A with reporters and audience members.

According to recent reports, the historic milestone isn’t without its drama. Voyager 1 has been in space for nearly half a century, and in that time, NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory has done everything it can to extend the life of Voyager 1. That includes troubleshooting concerns, performing maintenance, and shutting down various systems to save power and extend the spacecraft’s lifespan.

Sources indicate that several of those efforts took place in 2026. The team running Voyager 1 spent weeks shutting down three devices and powering on three low-power alternatives to reduce overall power usage. This initiative, which was internally called The Massive Bang, was also performed on Voyager 2. The transition was completed in early September, giving Voyager 1 more time with its dwindling power supply while also keeping it warm enough to continue operating in the frigid conditions of interstellar space.

It was a tricky maneuver that required the team to simultaneously turn multiple instruments on and off. The difficulty of the maneuver was amplified by the fact that it took almost a full day for any signal to reach Voyager and another full day for Voyager to send a signal back, with hours of downtime while the spacecraft performed the operations.

All of this took place several months after Voyager 1 experienced a sudden drop in power, which necessitated shutting off one of its three remaining instruments still in operation. Voyager 1 now has only two instruments still in operation.

Sources indicate that making it a whole light-day away from Earth is likely going to be Voyager 1’s final milestone while it still has enough power to communicate with Earth. Voyager 1 is powered by three radioisotope thermoelectric generators. They are essentially nuclear-powered batteries that generate energy by converting the steady heat from decaying plutonium-238.

Industry observers note that when Voyager 1 first debuted, its radioisotope thermoelectric generators produced about 470 watts of power. But plutonium-238 doesn’t last forever, and after 50 years in space, the RTGs now produce about 215 watts of power, with an average loss of about 4 watts per year. Most of that power is used to keep Voyager 1 up and running, which is why NASA has shut down eight of the 10 instruments that Voyager had when it launched.

At its current rate of usage and decay, Voyager 1 is expected to shut down its final science instrument in the 2030s and will eventually lose communication with Earth in 2036 due to insufficient power to send back a radio signal.

It has been revealed that the same fate is expected for Voyager 2, Voyager 1’s twin, which has also spent half a century in space. While it is labeled the sequel, Voyager 2 actually launched 16 days before Voyager 1, and the two have spent nearly identical amounts of time traversing the cosmos. Thanks to its slower speed and trajectory, it likely won’t reach the one light-day distance until after its instruments shut down.

Recent findings suggest that thanks to the vastness of space, Voyager 1 will lose all of its power before it hits its next milestone, which is the beginning of the Oort Cloud, a vast, icy shell of comets at the edge of our solar system. It’ll take about 300 years for Voyager 1 to make it there.

It has been revealed that thanks to the near-perfect vacuum of outer space, Voyager 1 will continue to fly at its current speed even after it shuts down entirely. So it’ll still hit that milestone; it just won’t be able to phone home to tell us about it.

  • In a recent development, with many of today’s laptops, you can leave the charger at home for days at a time.
  • Recent findings suggest that this increase in battery life is one of the biggest stories in laptops this year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I can almost guarantee that your next laptop will run longer on battery power than whatever you’re presently using. We’ve seen a huge leap in laptop battery life in recent years, to the point where getting 20 or more hours on a single charge isn’t uncommon. This year alone, the average battery life of the laptops we’ve tested at CNET has increased by more than five hours. And it’s nearly doubled since the start of the decade.

In a recent development, with many of today’s laptops, you can leave the charger at home for days at a time. The longest-lasting laptop I tested this year lasted more than 34 hours!

Recent findings suggest that this increase in battery life is one of the biggest stories in laptops this year. In the laptop episode of our video series Holiday Office Hours From the Labs, I explain what’s behind this surge in battery life and highlight some of the laptops that lasted the longest in testing.

Plus, my colleagues Kyle Kucharski from ZDNET and Joe Osborne from PCMag share their own holiday laptop picks. Kyle looks at Apple’s entry-level MacBook Neo and its imitators, and Joe breaks down what to look for in a budget gaming laptop.

Unlike raw performance, where the more you spend, the more you get, lengthy battery life can be found just as easily in a budget laptop as in an expensive, high-end powerhouse. And, in fact, less powerful components and lower screen resolutions can give cheaper laptops an edge in battery life.

Recent findings suggest that the biggest factor behind longer battery life in laptops is the advancement in mobile processors. They’ve become much more power efficient, and in the case of Apple’s and Qualcomm’s chips, they’re based on an architecture other than the traditional x86 instruction set that’s been at the heart of Intel processors since the dawn of the PC era.

Apple’s run of battery-life winners started when it shifted from Intel processors to its own M-series chips. Apple’s M-series processors are based on the Arm architecture, a power-efficient chip architecture found in phones and tablets. Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X-series processors are also Arm-based, and they can be found in the two longest-running laptops we’ve tested: the HP OmniBook 3 16 and OmniBook 5 14. The OmniBook 3 16’s record-setting battery performance earned it a CNET Lab Award for longest battery life.

Sources indicate that intel has made huge strides in processor efficiency with its last two generations of chips: the Core Ultra 200 series developed under the name Lunar Lake, and the Core Ultra 300 series, also known as Panther Lake. Last year, the Lenovo Yoga 9i 2-in-1 Aura Edition became the first Intel laptop to last longer than a day, running for 25 hours, 45 minutes in testing. It’s still the longest-running Intel laptop we’ve tested, but the MSI Prestige 14 Flip AI Plus with Intel’s next-gen Core Ultra X7 358H processor came close with a time of 25 hours, 18 minutes.

Read more: Laptops With the Best Battery Life.

Industry observers note that whether Arm or x86, there are two more reasons behind greater processor efficiency and longer laptop battery life. For one, the size of a processor shrinks with every generation. The smaller a processor is and the more tightly packed its components are, the less power is required to flip its tinier transistors on and off. For another, today’s mobile processors feature more flexible designs with a mix of performance and efficiency cores. A processor engages its higher-performance cores only when needed, using the efficiency cores for as many general, everyday tasks as possible, so your laptop stays cool and quiet and runs longer.

For more, you can read my Labs exclusive on the huge increase in laptop battery life this year and check out the video above for my holiday laptop picks and those from my colleagues.

By David Dierking – Nov 18, 2026 at 7:00AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Vanguard S&P 500 ETF ›.

Many people view a bear market as an opportunity to sell stocks. After all, if the market is about to drop 20% or more, why would you want your portfolio to ride it on the way down?

In a recent development, the reason is that no one knows if or when a bear market might arrive. In the end, many folks thought the declines would continue after stocks and long-term Treasuries both fell more than 20% at the same time. Instead, the S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.33%) posted three straight years of double-digit gains, bigger gains for tech stocks, and another 11% year-to-date gain in 2026.

That's why Warren Buffett advocates a simple, long-term buy-and-hold approach for most investors, using the S&P 500. Even during bear markets, holding and continuing to accumulate shares of the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -0.01%) has been the best strategy for maximizing the opportunities presented in severe drawdowns.

Former Berkshire CEO Warren Buffett. Image source: Getty Images.

In 2013, Warren Buffett famously suggested that for his wife's eventual inheritance, he instructed his advisor to put 90% of the money into an S&P 500 index fund ("I suggest Vanguard's.") and the remaining 10% in Treasury bills.

The logic is straightforward. An ultra-low-cost S&P 500 index fund provides broad exposure to the U.S. economy's biggest companies and allows participation in their long-term growth stories. The cash position gives you the means to fund additional purchases in your portfolio, ideally at lower prices, and does so without requiring you to sell stocks at a loss.

NYSEMKT · As of 9:37 AM ET 11/18/26.

There's a big difference between weakness in individual companies and weakness in the economy.

When there's a recession, all companies are affected, even the largest and most successful. But that doesn't mean the long-term fundamental strength of these companies has necessarily changed. The economic environment as a whole goes through a period of weakness, as it does from time to time. Sometimes the economy is strong. Sometimes it's not. It's normal behavior when you own something economically sensitive.

In a recent development, it's because these swings are normal that you want to hold the S&P 500 throughout them. If a firm is on the path to bankruptcy, you have a case for selling that stock. But you don't want to essentially sell off the entire U.S. economy because it's going through a temporary period of weakness. You get the good and the bad when you invest in stocks, and that's why long-term buy-and-hold is so important. This is Buffett's point of view as well.

It has been revealed that the best approach is usually to just keep doing what you're doing. Avoid the temptation to sell because you see stock prices going down. Keep contributing to your investment accounts monthly. Make sure your portfolio allocation aligns with your personal goals.

Buffett's past statements suggest that the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF would be the ideal product to accomplish this.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • An estimated 1.5 million travelers had their flight aims upended on Friday, Nov.
  • That ground stop lifted at 8:15 p.m.
  • In a recent development, nerdWallet travel writer Craig Joseph was among those affected.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An estimated 1.5 million travelers had their flight aims upended on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, after the Federal Aviation Administration announced a rare nationwide ground stop. That number comes from the flight data firm Cirium, which tracked passengers scheduled to depart U.S. airports that day after the stop was declared. The ground stop lasted more than four hours.

That ground stop lifted at 8:15 p.m. ET on Friday, but the ripple effects could be massive. Planes are out of position for the weekend, and some travelers are still trying to reach their destinations or get refunds on flights and other expenses.

In a recent development, nerdWallet travel writer Craig Joseph was among those affected. He was flying out of Asheville, North Carolina, for a one-night trip to a college football game, and learned his flight was delayed by three hours. Because it was a quick trip, and he had booked with frequent flyer miles that could be redeposited into his account, he canceled. Moments later, his flight — and every other one on the departures board — was canceled.

He canceled his hotel before the deadline, too, so his only sunk cost was the football ticket. But not all travelers will be so lucky.

If your travel plans were impacted, here's how you can get your money back.

Don’t count on calling customer service. Major airlines have been overwhelmed with customers asking for help.

In a recent development, as of Friday night, Southwest’s automated phone number stated it would take several hours to get a callback from a human. American Airlines’ automated line said it would take at least two hours to reach a human. Frontier Airlines wouldn’t even let us speak to a human, and instead sent us to a chatbot.

Industry observers note that skip the chatbots and long waits. Instead, do this:.

Check the airline’s app or website, and look for any emails or other alerts. Most airlines are proactively notifying affected passengers with rebooking options, and you may be automatically rebooked.

Get a refund or rebook online or through the airline's app. Every major airline has issued a travel waiver due to the ground stop, which gives you more flexibility to rebook without a change fee, often without charging for fare differences. More on that below.

Check your travel insurance. Because the ground stop was outside the airlines' control, they may not offer vouchers for hotels or food. If you paid these costs out of pocket, you might be able to get reimbursed from your travel insurance policy, if you purchased one, or your card's coverage. More on that below, too.

According to recent reports, under U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) rules, you are entitled to a full refund if your flight is canceled or significantly delayed — no matter the reason — and you decide not to travel and turn down other forms of compensation like travel credits. The money must be delivered to your original payment method, even if you bought nonrefundable tickets.

Industry observers note that if your flight disruption meets the DOT criteria, make sure you're getting a full refund. Some airline waivers offer a travel credit as a default option. Credits typically expire, and you won't get value from them until you redeem them. With a refund, you can get your money back within days.

If you booked with points or miles, you'll generally get those redeposited to your loyalty account, plus a refund of any taxes and fees you paid.

But if you still want to forge on with your travels, most airlines are allowing affected passengers to rebook fresh flights without owing a change fee or fare difference, which is more generous than usual. If your original travel dates were Nov. 13 or 14, and you purchased your tickets on or before Nov. 12 or 13, you're likely eligible for these flexible change policies.

Recent findings suggest that depending on the airline, you might have even more flexibility. For example, Southwest’s more generous rebooking policy applies to flights scheduled through Monday, Nov. 16.

Just note that each airline has its own limitations on when you must take that latest flight, so check with your airline to ensure you book within the allowed window. Here are the waiver pages for major airlines:.

Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines.

Sources indicate that right now, you and everyone else who was supposed to be on that Friday afternoon flight are vying for limited seats on aircraft flying the same route over the next few days. Get creative if the flight you need is booked up. Think about whether a nearby airport might be possible. You might also opt for a train or rental car.

If your flight disruption also cost you a hotel night, a rental car, a concert or sports ticket, or some other prepaid piece of your trip, here's your best chance at getting that money back, too:.

Industry observers note that call the hotel or rental property directly. Although not guaranteed, your host may waive a cancellation penalty or no-show fee for a documented flight disruption like this one. Have your canceled or delayed flight confirmation handy, and ask kindly.

For nonrefundable event tickets like concerts or sports games, you’re unlikely to get a direct refund. Check the specific event's refund policy first (and it never hurts to ask!), but your best bet in most cases is reselling the ticket through a platform like StubHub, SeatGeek or Vivid Seats rather than counting on a refund from the original seller.

Keep every receipt and email confirmation. Whether you're asking a hotel for an exception or filing an insurance claim, having your original flight confirmation, the cancellation or delay notice and your other prepaid reservations documented in one place will make every one of these conversations faster.

According to recent reports, if you have a standalone travel insurance policy: Travel delay and missed connection benefits may cover you for a disruption like this one, according to the insurance marketplace Squaremouth. If you already hold a policy, contact your provider's 24-hour emergency assistance line directly rather than waiting to file a claim after the fact.

Industry observers note that if you don't think you bought travel insurance, check your card terms. Many premium travel credit cards include travel insurance for covered events as a card benefit, assuming you paid for the trip with your card. But in this case, trip cancellation and interruption coverage likely wouldn't apply, because covered events are limited to things like illness, injury and inclement weather.

Recent findings suggest that but trip delay coverage (which typically applies after a delay of 6 to 12 hours) often covers "equipment failure," so it's more likely to apply here — if the ground stop is deemed to be an equipment failure. This coverage would reimburse "reasonable" expenses during a delay, like meals and lodging. Save your receipts so you're ready to file a claim, but keep in mind that card terms vary and the claim might be denied.

The backlog from Friday's ground stop is expected to keep disrupting flights through the weekend. If you have a flight in the coming days, recheck your specific flight status before heading to the airport even if things looked fine an hour ago.

Sources indicate that and whatever you were counting on — a refund, a rebooking or an insurance payout — make sure you move fast, document everything and don't assume you only have one option. With airline waivers, DOT refund rules and travel insurance, you might have more ways to get your money back than you think.

As for Joseph, he’s still trying to resell his football ticket.

According to recent reports, in the third quarter, Bloom Energy burned $181 million in free cash flow, while GE Vernova generated $5.4 billion, well above its GAAP net income of $1.3 billion. The difference comes down to a crucial measure investors shouldn't overlook: working capital.

In capital-intensive businesses, profits are part of the story. How effectively a firm turns day-to-day operations into cash can tell us much more. Here's what investors should know about this key difference between GE Vernova and Bloom Energy right now.

Sources indicate that in the past couple of years, GE Vernova and Bloom Energy have benefited from powerful tailwinds driven by an unprecedented demand for on-site, reliable power solutions. After decades of modest electricity demand growth, data centers, industrial reshoring, and grid electrification are driving strong electricity demand.

In Q3, GE Vernova booked $29 billion in orders for heavy-duty gas turbines and other power equipment, against $12.6 billion in total revenue, and its backlog grew to $197 billion. Because hyperscalers and utility customers pay upfront deposits to reserve factory slots, GE Vernova saw contract liabilities (deferred revenue) jump from around $26 billion to $46 billion in the first nine months of this year.

NYSE · As of 9:32 AM ET 11/18/26.

In a recent development, on top of this, GE Vernova takes longer to pay suppliers than it does to hold inventory. Taken together, when orders surge, cash flows into GE Vernova well before product is delivered. As a result, its non-cash working capital (which subtracts payables and contract liabilities from receivables, inventory, and contract assets) has fallen, contributing significantly to its $5.4 billion in free cash flow in the period.

Sources indicate that bloom Energy saw free cash flow come in at negative $181 million due to the opposite effect. That's because Bloom is manufacturing and installing solid-oxide fuel cells faster than it bills customers, partly because it has offered customer-friendly milestone-based billing tied to installation and commissioning, rather than requiring upfront payments.

As a result, unbilled work absorbs almost all of its customer inflow deposits, and fuel cells sitting in finished goods drain its cash balance until they are delivered and billed.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/17/26.

GE Vernova and Bloom Energy have been major beneficiaries of AI adoption, although both stocks are experiencing significant volatility as investors reevaluate the thesis around the size and speed of the data center build-out.

For GE Vernova, its negative non-cash working capital position provides a financial cushion, as customers and suppliers pay for its expansion, boosting near-term free cash flow that outpaces earnings growth and reducing the need to raise capital.

For Bloom Energy, its positive non-cash working capital means it relies on timely execution and customer payments to grow its cash position. The tech giant is spending heavily on manufacturing and expanding capacity, along with customer-friendly milestone-based billing, which is eating into free cash flow today despite surging profits.

Breaking: Vitalik Buterin Just Gave Ethereum Investors a Wake-Up Call. Here’s Why It Could Be Time to Sell.

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (644 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that if you bought Ethereum (ETH -1.61%) expecting the fees it uses to shrink its coin supply and lift its price, it might be time to sell.
  • Industry observers note that instead, he thinks it should be considered as a store of value, which implies different things about what makes it valuable.
  • Buterin's view is that rather than maximizing fee revenue, Ethereum should instead prioritize a group of properties that he calls CROPS: censorship and capture resistance, open-source code, privacy, and security.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Alex Carchidi – Nov 18, 2026 at 7:10AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Ethereum ›.

Industry observers note that if you bought Ethereum (ETH -1.61%) expecting the fees it uses to shrink its coin supply and lift its price, it might be time to sell. Its co-founder, Vitalik Buterin, just remarked not to count on that premise. In a Nov. 8 thread on X (formerly Twitter), Buterin said that his vision for the coin is that its value should be assessed by a handful of factors that are distinct from the fees owners pay to make transactions on its blockchain.

Industry observers note that instead, he thinks it should be considered as a store of value, which implies different things about what makes it valuable. Here's why that newly outlined philosophical position could be grounds to sell Ethereum if you hold it.

Buterin's view is that rather than maximizing fee revenue, Ethereum should instead prioritize a group of properties that he calls CROPS: censorship and capture resistance, open-source code, privacy, and security.

The CROPS properties, he argues, will imbue the token with a greater value than what would be possible by valuing the asset on the basis of what people are willing to pay to interact with it on the Ethereum blockchain. That's somewhat plausible, as they're rare traits that are hard to imitate, and that Ethereum is already well positioned to deliver.

Industry observers note that buterin additionally claims that to add weight to the proof of the coin's value, the network should try to host more tokenized real-world assets (RWAs), like Treasury bills held as a crypto token. Because those assets would be held on Ethereum, and because they could be exchanged for Ethereum or vice versa, the coin would be a medium of exchange, which would give it value even if the actual volume of exchanges taking place might be low.

CRYPTO · As of 9:34 AM ET 11/18/26.

But that portion of his argument is not very persuasive. On Jan. 1 of this year, there were $16.1 billion in tokenized assets on Ethereum's chain; as of Nov. 13, there were $15.1 billion. It doesn't appear as if the blockchain is a favored destination for fresh inflows related to tokenization, even though it's the crypto sector's leader in terms of its base of tokenized assets.

The wake-up call here is that Ethereum's most senior leadership has formally let go of the idea that the coin's price could be boosted over the long run by incurring transaction fees for its utilization and then burning some of those fees to destroy coins and constrain its supply.

It has been revealed that on some level, that makes sense, because the network's average fees per transaction have fallen by 96% during  the past five years as a result of tech upgrades. But for investors who bought the coin expecting fee burns to shrink its supply, it's now time to sell Ethereum. Adoption will still be pursued, but not as a way to maximize fee revenue; the CROPS factors are the priority, and their contribution to Ethereum's value is far harder to quantify than fee revenue and coins eliminated from the circulating supply.

For investors whose investment thesis was broader, it's also getting harder to argue for holding on, but the scale hasn't tipped yet, as Ethereum's financial weight within crypto still gives it a tremendous amount of staying power as well as growth potential.

#27398. 5 Brokerage Features We’re Excited for in 2027 (And 2 Things We Could Do Without)

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2308 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

5 Brokerage Features We’re Excited for in 2027 (And 2 Things We Could Do Without)

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2308 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Each fall, our investing team spends the latter half of the year hands-on testing a wide range of brokers, from legacy firms like Charles Schwab and Fidelity to newer, mobile-first firms like Public and M1.
  • This year, we opened or tested more than 15 brokerage accounts, funded them and placed real trades.
  • While our updated reviews and final star ratings are still in the works, here is a preview of five things that really stood out to us this season — and two things we’re feeling a bit wary of.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Each fall, our investing team spends the latter half of the year hands-on testing a wide range of brokers, from legacy firms like Charles Schwab and Fidelity to newer, mobile-first firms like Public and M1.

This year, we opened or tested more than 15 brokerage accounts, funded them and placed real trades. We sent each broker a detailed questionnaire covering more than 65 data points and then verified, categorized and scored their responses using our proprietary scoring system. And finally, though our team is spread across the U.S., we met in person to compare the experience of using each platform.

While our updated reviews and final star ratings are still in the works, here is a preview of five things that really stood out to us this season — and two things we’re feeling a bit wary of.

In a recent development, setting up buy and sell orders can be a pain point for some investors, especially beginners. Until recently, every platform required you to type in the ticker symbol, choose between dollars and shares, punch in the numbers and choose your order type. This creates opportunities for mistakes.

In recent months, AI has stepped in to help. Many platforms have debuted agents that you can ask to set up trades for you using natural language. Beginners aren’t the only people who benefit; some trading agents can also set up automated strategies based on prompts, thereby saving advanced traders a lot of time and effort monitoring the markets.

Public’s “Agents” feature, which started rolling out in March and became available to all owners in August, has become a trailblazer in agentic trading. It can place trades for you, set up recurring trades to automate a strategy (Managing Editor Chris Davis experimented with a “buy the open, sell the close” strategy for a while), and even sweep uninvested cash into one of Public’s high-yield cash management account options.

Industry observers note that robinhood also waded into the agentic trading space in early 2025 with the launch of its Cortex assistant, whose early iterations could place individual trades for you. In September of this year, the broker began rolling out Robinhood Agents, a more sophisticated natural-language interface that can build automated strategies based on a prompt, similar to Public’s Agents.

Interactive Brokers also offers a simple AI agent (IBot) that can set up trades for you, as does Cash App (Moneybot), but these are limited to one-time actions and cannot automate more complex strategies. Still, they can simplify the trading experience for beginners. That might be especially valuable to Cash App users, given the platform’s “My First Brokerage” ethos.

— Samuel Taube, Lead Investing Writer.

Recent findings suggest that » Curious about trading with a text prompt? Compare brokers with AI trading tools.

There’s been another profound shift in the past year that involves AI: agents that can actually help you manage your brokerage account. So far, some of the newer, mobile-first platforms seem to have an edge over the long-established financial behemoths. It’s also a mind-bending gray area: If an AI is giving you portfolio advice, who’s accountable for the advice it gives? Can you trust it? And how is it any different from a robo-advisor?

In our reviews this year, we looked into these questions. But here's a quick look at how one platform in particular is approaching this newly introduced frontier.

According to recent reports, from my testing over the years, I was already a huge fan of M1’s portfolio-building system, and now that it's integrated an AI advisor into the app (to be specific, M1 bills it as an SEC-registered AI fiduciary investment advisor legally required to act in your best interest), M1 has created what I truly think is a one-of-a-kind product and service. I checked the forms M1 is required to submit to the SEC, and the company declares outright that the AI advisor looks at your entire financial situation and gives actionable recommendations. In my experience with the app, those recommendations are based on your balances, the knowledge you provide and the ongoing conversations you have. There’s a lot to discuss here, which we’ll cover in our full M1 review, but suffice it to say, this is very impressive.

Industry observers note that most brokers don’t charge many fees these days. Trading, inactivity and account fees have slowly but surely disappeared, making investing more affordable over the years. But there is one fee you still have to pay: an expense ratio.

Recent findings suggest that most of the time, brokers have little control over expense ratios, since they’re set by fund managers. The only way a broker could offer an index fund without an expense ratio is if it was substantial enough to eat the cost.

This is exactly what Fidelity did back in 2018, when they introduced their “ZERO” funds. These funds have no expense ratios and no minimums, meaning they’re totally free for investors.

Fidelity remained the only broker to offer this kind of fund until 2025, when E*TRADE introduced a very similar lineup of no-expense-ratio index funds. The suite of funds from both brokers is fairly broad — think large-cap, total market, international — which makes them especially attractive to beginners building a portfolio from scratch.

Now, you may be wondering why these brokers decided to stray from the industry standard and offer products that don’t make them money. The idea is that the free funds will get you in the door — since you can only buy them if you have an account with that particular broker — and you’ll spend money on some other product they offer.

According to recent reports, but does that make free index funds any less great? No. I still think it’s a big step toward making investing more accessible for everyone, and I’m excited to see which brokers might add a similar offering in the future.

— Bella Avila, Investing Editor.

» Take a closer look: Compare Fidelity's and E*TRADE's free index funds.

In a recent development, I'm a big believer in putting every dollar to work, but that goal can sometimes fall through the cracks. Idle cash sitting uninvested in your brokerage account is a common oversight. It can easily pile up if you forget to reinvest sale proceeds or dividends (something I do more often than I’d like to admit). Or maybe you leave it parked for too long in your brokerage’s default account while waiting on a good investment opportunity.

Thankfully, most brokerages offer some form of interest on that uninvested money. Some put the idle funds in a money market fund, which can offer yields that mirror market rates. Others “sweep” your unused cash into partner banks to take advantage of FDIC insurance.

Recent findings suggest that in today’s environment, people with money in savings vehicles like high-yield savings accounts or new CDs are well-positioned to take advantage of high rates. What sets some brokerages apart is whether they operate similarly. That is, do they raise rates in response to larger economic circumstances? And if so, how promptly?

Robinhood and Public are two firms on our radar that are offering competitive rates in response to hikes, ranging from 3.6% to 3.75% as of this writing. Robinhood requires a premium subscription to unlock those higher rates, while Public’s already high base rate of 3.3% applies to all customers and can be boosted to 3.75% with a Reserve membership. For investors who keep a lot of cash in their account, the extra fee can be worth it.

In a recent development, interest rates, of course, shouldn’t be the main reason you pick one broker over another. Costs, the types of securities available and platform usability are better starting points. But when a company meets those expectations and also offers a compelling interest rate on your uninvested money, it’s worth taking a closer look.

— Sabrina Parys, Investing Editor.

» See which brokers pay the most on idle cash: Best brokerages for high interest rates.

In a recent development, direct indexing is a strategy in which you replicate an existing stock index (like the S&P 500, for example) but customize it how you like. The most popular reason people choose direct indexing is for tax optimization — but it’s not the only one.

Recent findings suggest that direct indexing can also be used to avoid overexposure to a specific company. For instance, if you work at Apple and get company stock, you probably don’t need even more exposure to Apple through the S&P 500. Direct indexing lets you replace that one stock with a similar company instead.

According to recent reports, and then there’s the reason direct indexing appealed to me: it lets you avoid buying into companies you just don’t support. I’m sure we all invest in companies we don’t necessarily mesh with morally, but direct indexing can help you avoid that.

The strategy used to be available only to people with an advisor managing their investment account, and they had to have millions to get started. More recently, these minimums have dropped. And now, it’s not just for people with financial advisors — online brokers offer the strategy, too.

According to recent reports, while some brokers still have steep minimums of $100,000 or so, others let you get started with less. Fidelity, in true Fidelity fashion, started offering direct indexing to clients a few years ago through a managed portfolio that has a minimum investment requirement of only $5,000.

In a recent development, I was pleased to see Public launch direct indexing with a minimum of only $1,000 a year ago. However, we should note that with a low investment amount, you can only track a portion of an index.

But even with those limitations, I think it’s great that these companies are putting out the message that there shouldn’t be a huge barrier to entry to customize your portfolio. As direct indexing continues to gain popularity, we’ll be watching whether more brokers start offering it, as advancements in AI undoubtedly make it easier to do so.

— Bella Avila, Investing Editor.

It’s hard to ignore the rise of prediction markets in the mainstream. These days, it takes just a few clicks to bet on who might win the Super Bowl or take home a Grammy. These markets, which operate on contracts with binary outcomes, are easy to access and use everyday language, making them all the more tempting to try — and now they are beginning to appear on many broker platforms and apps.

We’d like to be clear on this one: Our editors have no intention of telling you how to spend your extra discretionary money. If you have a solid financial foundation and have allocated a few bucks to bet on some event contracts, that’s all good. But as editors who view investing apps as vehicles for legitimate wealth-building strategies, we draw the line at these products being marketed alongside other investments, such as stocks, ETFs and mutual funds.

In fact, this year we’ve actually decided to dock points in our annual reviews and ratings from brokerages that offer unrestricted access to event and sports-style prediction markets. In our view, these products aren’t conducive to long-term investing, and they’re speculative without enough oversight — a troublesome combination. You can read more about our stance and why we’re taking it here.

— Sabrina Parys, Investing Editor.

I’d venture to say that since the dawn of social media, people have been talking about investing online. And nowadays, the online investing community is huge. The r/investing subreddit has more than 3.5 million followers, and even on a video-forward platform like TikTok, #investing has 4.1 million posts under it.

But is where people go to talk about investing online changing?

Sources indicate that the first broker I saw incorporate a social media–style element into its platforms was etoro. When you scroll down on the app's “home” tab, you’re met with what looks like an X feed. And the CopyTrader feature lets you copy another person’s portfolio, with that section of the app highlighting “trending investors,” “market outperformers,” and more.

This wasn’t a huge surprise to me coming from a niche broker with presumably a large user base of active traders. What surprised me was when Robinhood added a social media-style section to its app, testing a beta version in March and expanding it to all U.S. consumers in October.

Sources indicate that robinhood Social is, again, much like an X feed but for showing people which stocks you’re buying or selling. When I created an account to see what it was all about, the app encouraged me to share my “stats” on my profile (my one-day and one-year profit and loss, and my profit rate). “Trading stats build trust and transparency on Social,” the app said.

Sources indicate that you could argue that other, even bigger brokers promote social trading. Fidelity, for example, has a “customer orders” section that demonstrates how many Fidelity users are buying and selling certain stocks (though, I’ll say, they don’t promote this feature and it’s buried in the app).

It has been revealed that the huge difference, in my opinion, is that Fidelity leaves it up to you to research these stocks. There’s no feed or comment section. On etoro and Robinhood, people can say whatever they want about why they bought or sold a certain security — whether truthful or not — or worse, why you should or shouldn’t invest in something.

To me, the whole concept of social trading feels like the antithesis of long-term investing. It’s a trend that I hope we don’t see becoming more popular among major-name brokers.

— Bella Avila, Investing Editor.

Disclosure: Neither the authors nor the editor owned any of the aforementioned investments at the time of publication.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Erin Kennedy – Updated Nov 18, 2026 at 7:11AM EST.
  • Industry observers note that investors today can choose between the massive cash generation of a global financial exchange and the high-growth disruption of an AI lending platform.
  • CME Group provides the critical infrastructure for global risk management, while Upstart uses advanced technology to redefine personal credit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Erin Kennedy – Updated Nov 18, 2026 at 7:11AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than CME Group ›.

Industry observers note that investors today can choose between the massive cash generation of a global financial exchange and the high-growth disruption of an AI lending platform. Is CME Group (CME -0.46%) or Upstart (UPST +1.10%) the better buy?

CME Group provides the critical infrastructure for global risk management, while Upstart uses advanced technology to redefine personal credit. While both companies operate within the financial services sector, they offer very different risk and reward profiles. Comparing their recent performance and valuation can help you decide which stock fits your 2027 goals.

In its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, CME Group describes its position as the world's leading derivatives marketplace. The manufacturer provides essential trading and clearing services across major asset classes. Key partnerships include a strategic 10-year cloud infrastructure deal with Alphabet (GOOGL +1.62%) (GOOG +1.06%) and a prediction markets joint venture with Flutter Entertainment (FLUT -0.28%). In 2025, one clearing firm accounted for nearly 12% of total clearing and transaction fees. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

In a recent development, reliable recent quarterly figures for at least one of these companies aren't available, so this comparison uses each organization's latest full fiscal year. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, revenue reached nearly $6.5 billion, representing 6.4% growth over the previous fiscal year. Net income for the period was close to $4 billion. This high level of profitability stems from the company's vital role in global financial markets.

As of CME's December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 0.1. This low ratio shows that total debt is only a small fraction of shareholder equity. The current ratio of roughly 1 measures the ability to cover short-term debts with short-term assets. Free cash flow was approximately $4.2 billion in fiscal 2025. This metric represents the cash remaining after a business covers its operating expenses and capital expenditures.

Industry observers note that upstart operates an AI-powered lending marketplace that aims to modernize traditional credit scoring. The tech giant connects individual borrowers with more than 100 bank and credit union partners. Its business relies on high-traffic aggregators like Credit Karma to attract new applicants to the platform. This ecosystem currently places the company among the most innovative fintech stocks in the market today.

In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, Upstart reported revenue of approximately $1 billion. This represented a substantial 64% increase compared to the prior 12-month period. The firm also returned to profitability, reporting net income of nearly $53.6 million. This turnaround highlights the potential scalability of its AI-driven lending model.

In a recent development, as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 2.3. This means total liabilities are more than double the organization's shareholder equity. The current ratio was approximately 3, indicating the company has three times more short-term assets than short-term liabilities. Free cash flow for the period was negative $166.1 million.

CME Group faces risks from global market volatility and fluctuations in trading volumes. Its reliance on technology infrastructure makes it susceptible to cybersecurity threats, such as the cooling failure at a CyrusOne data center in late 2025. The organization also deals with intense competition from rivals like Intercontinental Exchange (ICE -0.12%) and Cboe Global Markets (CBOE -0.95%). Licensing agreements with benchmark providers such as S&P Global (SPGI -0.36%) also present ongoing intellectual property risks.

In a recent development, upstart is highly dependent on a limited number of lending partners and institutional investors for loan funding. Plus, payments, identity verification, and security remain important to the shopping experience.

In January 2026, PayPal unveiled collaborations with Microsoft to power Copilot Checkout and with Alphabet to support Google's Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP).

Beyond that, PayPal has been expanding its capabilities through its agreement to acquire Cymbio, a commerce orchestration platform that helps merchants make their products available across AI-driven shopping channels.

Looking ahead, if this upcoming shopping model gains widespread adoption, PayPal could benefit from a new source of payment activity while helping merchants reach customers across multiple digital platforms.

With that, PayPal is pursuing these newer opportunities alongside its broader push to make its existing consumer and merchant businesses more profitable.

By David Dierking – Nov 18, 2026 at 7:30AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

Industry observers note that recession headlines tend to trigger very emotional responses from investors. They often suggest the worst is coming and give the impression that you have to do something now or risk losing even more money.

In a recent development, while that feeling is understandable, studies have shown that doing nothing actually produces some of the best results. A recent DALBAR study found that the average investor in both equity and fixed income funds over a two-decade period significantly trailed their index benchmarks.

The reason usually cited for this is over-trading and market timing. Investors often sell after losses have already occurred and don't buy back until the recovery is already in progress. As a result, they miss out on performance gains.

Here's why long-term buy-and-hold is the one strategy that succeeds over and over.

Industry observers note that the U.S. economy has gone through numerous recessions, generational economic crises, and bear markets over the past century. The stock market has fallen sharply in nearly all of them. Yet every time in history, the S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.33%) has recovered and reached a latest all-time high.

That's the major difference between short-term volatility and long-term growth. The U.S. economy is cyclical. It'll go through periods of expansion and contraction, and of asset prices rising and falling. That's a normal part of investing in assets that come with risk, and it should be expected.

But the long-term trajectory of the U.S. economy has been up. Gross domestic product, the number of people employed, household incomes, and corporate earnings have all continued to rise over time. Those are the factors that matter most. When investing for the long term, you should focus on these decades-long uptrends, not the short-term ups and downs that occur along the way. The only way to capture those uptrends is to stay invested throughout these cycles.

It has been revealed that that doesn't just mean that investors can or should put their money in anything. The core of any equity portfolio should be built around durable, high-quality companies that can withstand a range of market and economic environments. Some of the more speculative or emerging companies could go bankrupt in their first adverse economic environment. But the substantial, quality companies with healthy balance sheets should be able to survive economically weak periods.

These companies tend to share a few common traits:.

But one of the only ways to consistently take advantage of these characteristics is to stay invested. Let the long-term compounding of growth do the work for you.

5 Student Loan Scams to Avoid in 2026

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (972 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that student loan scams can be costly, but they usually leave clues.
  • Sources indicate that the communication might seem realistic, but unexpected fees, unknown contacts and massive promises are usually red flags.
  • Here’s a breakdown of common student loan scams and what to do about them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that student loan scams can be costly, but they usually leave clues. Scammers will often try to hook victims with tempting claims of “act now or miss out” and “we promise to get you student aid.".

Sources indicate that the communication might seem realistic, but unexpected fees, unknown contacts and massive promises are usually red flags. The age-old adage is true: if an offer sounds too good to be true, it probably is.

Here’s a breakdown of common student loan scams and what to do about them.

» MORE: How to spot student loan repayment scams.

The scam: A fraudulent private organization offers to manage your student loans and help you get them relieved or even fully forgiven. These services can cost more than $1,000, and there’s no guarantee that you’ll actually get the help you’re looking for.

How to avoid it: You can manage your federal student loans for free. According to the U.S. Department of Education, you never have to pay for help with your federal student loans[1]U.S. Department of Education. Avoiding Student Aid Scams. View all sources . You can work with your loan servicer to adjust your payment plan, consolidate loans and apply for loan forgiveness at no cost to you.

If you’re being promised immediate student loan forgiveness, are asked for personal identification information like your FAFSA login credentials or asked to authorize a power of attorney, proceed with caution — it’s likely a scam.

» MORE: How to get help with student loans.

According to recent reports, the scam: A company charges you an upfront fee to combine multiple student loans into one newly introduced loan to reduce your monthly payment. The company may be illegitimate and is likely to pocket the fee without actually consolidating your loans.

Recent findings suggest that how to avoid it: You can consolidate federal student loans for free. There is no fee to consolidate your loans through the Department of Education at studentaid.gov. If you’re looking to reduce your monthly payment through consolidation, start by contacting your loan servicer. And if you get unsolicited communication from a firm promising federal student loan consolidation, it's probably a scam.

The scam: Scammers use transitions in federal loan programs to take advantage of borrowers. For example, the Education Department was set to resume wage garnishments after a long pause, but in January 2026 declared a temporary delay implement repayment reforms.

When federal decisions go back and forth like this, it creates a gray area for scammers to make wage garnishment threats. For borrowers who may not know if wage garnishment restarted, it can be hard to know what to do. This goes for other federal changes, too; any uncertainty can be an opportunity for bad actors to take advantage of the confusion.

Recent findings suggest that how to avoid it: If your wages are truly being garnished, the communication will come from the federal government and not a private tech giant. Likewise, if a company offers to stop your wage garnishment for a fee, you’re probably getting scammed.

The scam: Criminals impersonate a real person and apply to colleges in their name. Then, they can collect financial aid, take out loans and use their college admission to net discounts on goods and services. This is known as a “ghost student” scam.

How to avoid it: Follow the steps on identitytheft.gov to report fraud and get a recovery proposal. There are a few safeguards you can put in place to prevent this form of identity theft, such as setting up a credit freeze and monitoring your FSA ID activity.

Sources indicate that how it works: You might receive a call from someone claiming to be from your school’s financial aid office saying you have unpaid tuition. The caller may threaten that you cannot start your classes until your tuition bill is paid in full. Scammers can be creative and convincing, even going so far as to replicate a school’s phone number to display on your caller ID.

How to avoid it: The Federal Trade Commission warns that schools will not call and pressure you to pay tuition[2]Federal Trade Commission. Got a call about unpaid college tuition? It could be a scam. Accessed Nov 16, 2026. View all sources . Rather than trust the caller, use your school's secure student portal to check your account balance. Know for certain what you owe and to whom before sending money. You can also call your financial aid office to confirm the legitimacy of a phone number that has called you requesting tuition funds.

In a recent development, realizing you’ve been scammed is stressful, and it’s natural to feel overwhelmed or embarrassed. But acting swiftly can make a real difference. The sooner you report what happened, the better your chances of limiting the financial damage and getting your accounts back on track. Here’s what to do:.

In a recent development, if you’ve already paid a scammer, report the problem to the bank that issued the payment. If you paid with a credit card, for instance, contact the company and tell them what happened. They may be able to freeze your account or reverse the transaction.

Reach out to your federal student loan servicer as well and report what happened. They can check to make sure no changes have been made to your account and, in the case that changes did occur, they can help you get your loan back on track.

Recent findings suggest that file complaints with the Education Department, the Federal Trade Commission and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. Filing complaints with these agencies helps hold scammers accountable, can result in enforcement action or business shutdowns, and in some cases may help you recover lost funds.
