📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ryan Vanzo – Nov 18, 2026 at 8:56AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

According to recent reports, the S&P 500 index (^GSPC +0.33%) is one of the most popular stock market indexes in the world. Roughly $16 trillion is invested globally in index funds and ETFs tracking the S&P 500. The Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO +0.27%) alone has $1.7 trillion in assets.

Charlie Munger, the longtime business partner of Warren Buffett, once claimed that "95% of people have no chance of beating the S&P 500 Index." But I'm not sure that advice is true in today's market. And there's one glaring reason why.

In a recent development, most investors believe that the S&P 500 is a diversified basket of stocks that captures the valuation of the entire U.S. economy spanning a broad range of industries and sectors. That's true, but only up to a point.

Recent findings suggest that during the dot-com bubble, technology stocks accounted for roughly one-third of the index. When the bubble burst, S&P 500 investors learned they weren't as diversified as they had believed.

The same proved true during the financial crisis, when financial stocks comprised roughly one-quarter of the entire index. When that bubble burst, the S&P 500's supposed diversification benefits proved less reliable than initially thought.

In a recent development, today, nearly half of the S&P 500's value is tied up in either AI stocks or companies that supply the AI industry. The math isn't perfect, as many AI stocks engage in many other business activities besides AI. But the lofty valuations of these companies are very much tied to their AI efforts. If the AI story stumbles, nearly half of the S&P 500 could see their valuations compress sharply.

"Artificial intelligence concentration is increasing, both across the economy and in investor portfolios," research from Franklin Templeton warns. "[I]nvestors are now considering how to best mitigate concentration risk without sacrificing the gains from AI, which include economywide productivity growth and potentially superior investment returns.".

Industry observers note that in almost all cases, sticking with an index fund tracking the S&P 500 is prudent, even during market peaks. If you had purchased shares of an S&P 500 index fund at the peak of every bubble in history, you'd still be sitting on a healthy long-term profit. That's the power of long-term thinking.

According to recent reports, the matter today is that the S&P 500 no longer functions like it did in the past. In past bubbles, peak industry concentrations ranged from 25% to 35%. Today's AI concentration hovers around 45%. The decline of a single industry, therefore, could drag down your entire portfolio.

Recent findings suggest that many long-term, risk-tolerant investors may do well sticking with their traditional index fund exposure. Risk-averse investors such as retirees and those on a fixed income, however, should reassess just how "diversified" their portfolios are. The S&P 500 remains a great index to track long term. But it's no longer the no-brainer investment it used to be.

Tech Report: Preparing For Changing ABA CPT Codes In 2027

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (928 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Juan Pablo Montoya is Founder and CEO of Solum Health, which automates insurance verification and prior authorization with AI.
  • When a code set changes, the first thing practice owners ask me is which codes are upcoming.
  • In a recent development, what hurts is a code that keeps its number and changes what it means.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Juan Pablo Montoya is Founder and CEO of Solum Health, which automates insurance verification and prior authorization with AI.

When a code set changes, the first thing practice owners ask me is which codes are upcoming. I understand why, but it’s the wrong place to start. A new code can’t really hurt you because your billing system has never seen it and will say so. Deleted codes are also noisy since the claim usually bounces within days.

In a recent development, what hurts is a code that keeps its number and changes what it means. That claim goes out clean, and you find out weeks later from a denial or an auditor’s question nobody on the team can answer.​.

On January 1, 2027, applied behavior analysis gets that kind of change. Speech therapy gets a big dose of the other kind.​.

In a recent development, the ABA Coding Coalition’s crosswalk spells out the ABA CPT code changes: six new codes, revised descriptors for 97151 through 97158 and two Category III codes deleted. The change that matters is 97155. Under the 2019 descriptors, it covered protocol modification by the behavior analyst, with or without directing a technician, so it was where the analyst’s own hands-on treatment got billed. Beginning in January, it will mean the analyst directing a technician, and the analyst’s direct treatment will get its own code (97173).​.

According to recent reports, in speech, 92507 is deleted on January 1. ASHA described 10 replacements across five clinical categories, each built as a base code for the first 30 minutes plus an add-on for every additional 15 minutes. The group code, 92508, is revised into a stand-alone code. Outside Medicare, each payer decides when to add the latest codes to its fee schedule.​.

Industry observers note that this is a data problem before it’s a billing problem. If your system treats a CPT code as a plain label, “97155” in July and “97155” in January are the same string, and nothing downstream knows they describe different work. A code is really a definition with a start date. An authorization approved under last year’s definition doesn’t carry over to this year’s on its own.​.

Sources indicate that the timing makes it worse. Most ABA authorizations I see run six months, so almost anything approved since midsummer will still be open in January. Those approvals funded 97155 hours that belong to two different codes from January 1, and unless the payer indicates otherwise in writing, the authorization won’t tell you how to split them.

Recent findings suggest that the claim to worry about is the one that pays. If an analyst keeps billing hands-on treatment as 97155 out of habit, it matches the old authorization and goes through, and it stays wrong until someone reads it against the 2027 definition. The speech authorizations I see are usually written as a number of 92507 visits, which in January becomes a count of visits for a code that no longer exists.​.

According to recent reports, don’t expect payer reporting to flag any of this for you. The largest Medicaid-managed care insurers denied 14% of standard prior authorization requests in 2025, and the published figures can’t show which services those were. If the cutover produces a run of mismatches, you’ll see it in your own data or not at all.​.

This should be a single query: every authorization ending after December 31 that references 97151 through 97158, 0362T, 0373T, 92507 or 92508. If it turns into a week of opening PDFs and reading notes fields, that’s your real finding.​.

Your code table needs start and end dates, so a December session is read against the 2026 definition and a January session against the 2027 one. Keep last year’s descriptors instead of overwriting them because sooner or later, someone will ask you to justify a 2026 claim. Load the crosswalk as reference data that your claim logic actually reads.​.

HIPAA-covered payers must accept code sets valid on the date of service, but each one decides when it will cover, price and authorize the upcoming codes. For a stretch, one payer may have 97173 loaded and priced while another hasn’t, so your system needs to know which payers have moved. Ask each one, in writing, how it will treat authorizations that cross January 1.​.

Sources indicate that splitting an authorization between technician direction and the analyst’s own treatment is a clinical call. Your behavior analysts have to make it, and the payer has to amend the authorization to match, ideally before the first January session.

While you’re asking, consider whether you also need the latest code for non-face-to-face analyst work, 97180, which no 2026 authorization could have listed. For speech teams, the equivalent job is turning approved visits into base and add-on units.​.

Industry observers note that set up a weekly view of rejections, denials and authorization mismatches on every new and revised code, and keep it running through February. Put paid 97155 claims in that view, too. Nobody reviews claims that paid, which is exactly where the habitual billing errors will sit.​.

Most of January’s coding problems will announce themselves with a rejection. The expensive one won’t; it’ll be a familiar number on an authorization you approved months ago now describing different work. I’d treat the cutover as a data migration rather than a coding patch, and I’d start that inventory now while payers still have time to process amendments.​.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that however, when stocks fall, not all tumble as much.
  • Here is what to look for in a dividend stock to help cushion the blow of a future stock market slump.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt DiLallo – Nov 18, 2026 at 9:03AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

The S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.33%) fell 4.4% on Nov. 5, its worst day since April 2025. It was another reminder of how swiftly stocks can tumble.

It has been revealed that however, when stocks fall, not all tumble as much. Research from Hartford Funds, using Ned Davis Research data, shows that since 1973 the stocks that held up better in big declines have been dividend payers. In market drawdowns of 10% or more, dividend-paying stocks fell 14.4%, versus 28.2% for non-dividend-paying stocks. That's about half as much.

Here is what to look for in a dividend stock to help cushion the blow of a future stock market slump.

It has been revealed that hartford Fund's analysis covers every S&P 500 drawdown of 10% or more from 1973 through 2025. In those periods, dividend-paying stocks fell an average of 14.4%. The equal-weighted S&P 500, a good proxy for the average stock, fell 19%. Meanwhile, stocks that didn't pay dividends tumbled 28.2%.

Industry observers note that in other words, dividend payers lost about half as much as non-payers during a stock market correction. While they still lost money, they helped preserve more wealth during a market downdraft.

Hartford suggested two reasons why dividend stocks tend to hold up much better than non-payers during a market downturn. Many dividend stocks tend to be concentrated in industries less sensitive to the economic cycle. For example, most consumer staples and utility stocks pay dividends because companies in these industries generate stable cash flow due to resilient demand.

Sources indicate that additionally, a tech giant typically needs to have a track record of profitability and relatively predictable cash flow before it initiates a dividend. That business maturity would also make a company's stock price less volatile.

While dividend payers have historically delivered higher total returns with less volatility than non-payers, one group of dividend stocks stood out from the pack:.

Sources indicate that companies that grew their dividends outperformed the average dividend stock and had lower volatility. Companies that cut or eliminated theirs lost money on average, with the most volatility of any group.

Industry observers note that hartford also found that the highest yields haven't been the best bet. Since 1930, stocks with the highest payout ratios (which typically have the highest yields) outperformed the market about half the time, similar to companies with much lower payout ratios. However, the sweet spot was companies with an average dividend payout ratio of 49%. These companies prioritized dividend payments while maintaining plenty of flexibility to continue growing their dividends even during more challenging times.

Those results point to a few simple ways to put the data to work before the next pullback.

Sources indicate that while dividend stocks have historically helped cushion the blow during downturns, that doesn't guarantee they will outperform during the next one. For example, S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats® (the term Dividend Aristocrats® is a registered trademark of Standard & Poor's Financial Services LLC) -- S&P 500 members with 25 or more years of annual dividend increases -- outperformed the market during the dot-com crash and global financial crisis. However, they underperformed during the COVID crash.

In a recent development, further, weaker companies tend to cut their dividends during periods of market stress. As we saw before, dividend cutters and eliminators have historically delivered negative total returns. That's why it's crucial to check a company's dividend payout ratio to ensure it has plenty of cushion to weather a market downturn.

When stocks tumble, history highlights dividend payers tend to fall about half as far as stocks that don't pay dividends, and dividend growers have done even better over time. It's a cushion, not a guarantee. If you're worried about a potential pullback, lean toward investing in companies with growing, well-covered dividends rather than non-payers and those with the highest yields.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Will Healy – Nov 18, 2026 at 9:22AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Palantir Technologies ›.

Palantir (PLTR -2.39%) has attracted considerable attention among businesses and investors alike in recent years. Its data analytics tools have driven eye-popping productivity gains for its clients. As such, interest in its products has soared, and annual revenue growth is approaching triple-digit percentages.

Unfortunately, this has also drawn attention to its valuation, as rapid revenue growth typically means a stock will trade at a considerable premium. Despite its impressive revenue growth, I believe Palantir stock is overvalued. Here's why.

Palantir began as a manufacturer focused on supporting national defense and intelligence agencies. Its tools employ artificial intelligence to analyze data and deliver insights. In its early days, the help it provided to U.S. intelligence services in finding Osama bin Laden gained the company considerable attention.

It has been revealed that however, seeing the limits of growth within that field, it turned its expertise to the commercial sector. While that broadening of its customer base led to increased growth, it was the release of its Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP) that was the game changer.

Palantir began offering potential customers the opportunity to enroll in “boot camps” where they were able to immediately see how AIP could be applied to their actual business problems, and as a result, many of its clients began to discover ways to use it to noticeably increase productivity.

In a recent development, among these companies is GE Aerospace, which applied AIP to fleet management and supply chain coordination, thereby increasing engine production. AIP also helped AIG automate insurance underwriting for more complicated commercial lines of business.

Such improvements helped drive Palantir’s revenue to nearly $5.9 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 92% from the prior-year period, with a blowout Q3 boosting that growth.

Sources indicate that moreover, since its costs and expenses grew more slowly than revenue, its net income was nearly $3.1 billion during the same period. That was a 201% year-over-year increase. Amid this performance, it is not too surprising that Palantir stock is up by more than 2,300% since the beginning of 2023.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/17/26.

According to recent reports, for 2026, revenue will grow 91% if the tech giant's forecasts hold. However, analysts predict that growth will slow to 53% in 2027.

Sources indicate that even though a 53% yearly revenue increase is still impressive, investors tend to frown on slowing growth. That could bode poorly for Palantir, particularly given its lofty valuation.

Palantir now trades at 110 times trailing earnings. Moreover, its forward P/E ratio of 92 is similarly pricey. When also considering the forward 1-year P/E ratio of 62, these metrics suggest Palantir's stock price has years of expected growth already baked into it.

It has been revealed that however, as high as these numbers sound, they also offer some hope to investors. The current stock price is around $165 per share as of this writing, a level it first reached in August 2025.

Recent findings suggest that at that time, its P/E ratio stood at 575, while its forward P/E and forward 1-year P/E were 239 and 102, respectively. Over the past year or so, its valuation ratios have eased down to somewhat more reasonable levels.

That may not bode well for near-term stock price gains, though, since its valuations remain high and the stock has been essentially trading sideways for 15 months. On the other hand, Palantir's rapid revenue growth and rising profitability dramatically reduce the odds of this SaaS stock suffering a steep correction, suggesting it is more of a hold than a sell.

Based on Palantir's financial metrics, the stock is overvalued, but that does not mean investors should necessarily dismiss it as a potential portfolio holding.

In a recent development, its stock price growth in recent years stemmed from the tech giant’s ability to deliver palpable productivity gains to its customers. That has led to massive revenue growth that prompted investors to bid the shares up to high valuations.

In a recent development, fortunately, Palantir's valuation has contracted somewhat in the past year. Since rapid revenue and profit growth have persisted, the stock offers current shareholders good reason to hold while also suggesting that future investors could buy at a lower premium. These factors alone make Palantir a stock that investors should continue to watch.

By Selena Maranjian – Nov 18, 2026 at 9:35AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.

Just about all of us know that Warren Buffett is one of the greatest investors ever, and many of us are familiar with the company he built into a trillion-dollar enterprise -- Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -1.02%) (BRKB -1.03%). He grew the company's value by nearly 20% annually over some 60 years!

Let's say you parked a modest $1,000 in Berkshire Hathaway 20 years ago. What would it be worth today? Well, the answer is $8,310. The shares would have been trading for around $71.29 per share in November 2006, and more recently, they've been around $590 apiece. That's a total gain of 732%, and an annualized one of 11.16% (which still tops the S&P 500's average of 9.3% over the same period).

According to recent reports, whenever I report these kinds of numbers, I like to include reinvested dividends. Berkshire is not a dividend-paying stock at this point, as its leaders have preferred to plow excess earnings into furthering its growth -- and they've occasionally repurchased some shares, too. The S&P 500 does feature dividends, though, and with dividends reinvested over 20 years, its average annual gain would come to 10.6% -- still below Berkshire's gain, but not by a lot.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/17/26.

Multiplying your investment's value eightfold is pretty great. Can you expect that kind of growth over the next 20 years with Berkshire? Well, maybe. I certainly wouldn't count on average annual gains of 20% or more, as the organization has delivered in the past -- because it can be especially hard for really large companies to grow.

But Berkshire is built to last, and features a lot of diversification. It owns many businesses in the insurance, energy, transportation, and manufacturing sectors, among others, and has a large portfolio of stocks, too. It's reasonable to hope or expect it to surpass the S&P 500's performance over the long run.

In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was nearly $5.3 billion, reinforcing its position among beverage stocks.

Monster Beverage develops and sells energy drinks, including Reign and NOS, and relies heavily on the Coca-Cola distribution network to reach 158 countries. Its primary customers include Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP -0.65%)and Coca-Cola Consolidated (COKE -0.30%), which account for roughly 15% and 10% of net sales, respectively. Such concentration adds a layer of risk to the business, as these two partners account for a significant share of distribution.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $9.6 billion, a significant growth of nearly 20.2% compared to the previous year. Net income for this period was roughly $2.2 billion. This expansion highlights the increasing consumer appetite for energy beverages and the company's ability to successfully scale its brands globally.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the manufacturer carries a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.0x, indicating it has no total debt relative to its equity. The current ratio is approximately 3.7x, suggesting a very strong ability to meet short-term financial obligations. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow reached nearly $2.0 billion. This financial flexibility allows for continued reinvestment into new product lines.

Recent findings suggest that coca-Cola faces pressure from global economic volatility and geopolitical instability that can disrupt its complex supply chain. The company must navigate intense competition from rivals such as PepsiCo (PEP -3.01%)and Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP -0.37%). Additionally, it manages ongoing tax litigation with the IRS and regulatory scrutiny regarding sugar-sweetened beverage taxes and environmental impacts of packaging.

Monster Beverage is vulnerable to category-specific regulations, such as potential age restrictions or limits on caffeine content in energy drinks. The organization relies heavily on the Coca-Cola distribution system, meaning any strategic shift by its partner could impact market access. Furthermore, it faces increasing competition from nimble competitors such as Celsius Holdings (CELH -1.24%)and rising costs for raw materials like aluminum.

Monster Beverage carries a higher Forward P/E and P/S ratio, which divides market cap by sales over the past twelve months, than Coca-Cola.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

Recent findings suggest that when comparing Coca-Cola and Monster Beverage, investors should consider a few key factors. Let's have a look at them and see what that tells us about each stock.

In a recent development, firstly, we should consider revenue growth. In this category, Monster gains a real edge. Over the last three years, it has averaged 11.8% year-over-year revenue growth, while Coca-Cola has averaged about 4.9%. Moreover, in recent quarters, Monster's revenue growth has surged well above its average, clocking in at 16.7% in its most recent quarter. Coca-Cola has also delivered above-average revenue growth, at 7% in its most recent report.

Another factor to consider is each company's profitability. Over the last 10 years, Coca-Cola has had an average operating margin of 27.1%, while Monster's was 31.7%, seemingly giving Monster the edge here. However, in recent years, Monster's profitability has drifted lower, while Coca-Cola's has increased. In fact, Coca-Cola has now overtaken Monster. Coca-Cola's operating margin is now 32.1%, while Monster's has fallen to 28.5%, giving Coca-Cola an advantage in this category.

Industry observers note that finally, there's valuation. Since both companies are profitable, it makes sense to compare their price-to-earnings (P/E) multiples. Coca-Cola has a P/E multiple of 29x, while Monster's is 40x. That gives Coca-Cola another edge, as its stock is more affordable.

To sum up, investors may want to consider both of these consumer stocks. However, given its more reasonable valuation and its higher profitability, Coca-Cola wins the battle between these two beverage giants, in my opinion. Nevertheless, given its impressive revenue growth, solid profitability, and reasonable valuation, Monster also remains a stock worth considering.

IonQ Stock Plunged 48% in Six Months. Is It a Bargain Buy?

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (737 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Shares of IonQ (IONQ -6.09%) are down about 48% over the past six months as investors have headed for the exits amid worries the company is spending too much on acquisitions and raising too much capital at the expense of existing shareholder value.
  • IonQ has always been a speculative bet on an unproven market — quantum computing — but some investors may wonder whether the recent share price pullback makes IonQ stock a bargain right now.
  • Unfortunately, even with the recent drop, its shares still aren't in the bargain bin.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Chris Neiger – Nov 18, 2026 at 9:47AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than IonQ ›.

Shares of IonQ (IONQ -6.09%) are down about 48% over the past six months as investors have headed for the exits amid worries the company is spending too much on acquisitions and raising too much capital at the expense of existing shareholder value.

IonQ has always been a speculative bet on an unproven market — quantum computing — but some investors may wonder whether the recent share price pullback makes IonQ stock a bargain right now.

Unfortunately, even with the recent drop, its shares still aren't in the bargain bin. Here's why investors are betting on IonQ, what the manufacturer has going for it, and why IonQ stock still isn't a good deal.

The biggest reason for IonQ's recent share price drop was the October announcement that the company would acquire Elisity, a zero-trust cybersecurity company. IonQ said it would make the $1.2 billion acquisition in an all-stock deal, diluting existing shareholders.

IonQ unveiled just a few days later that it was holding a $2 billion equity offering, cementing investors' concerns about share dilution. By the end of the month, IonQ's stock was down 31%.

According to recent reports, this decline came months after IonQ's shares tumbled over the summer as investors fled riskier tech stocks. The AI trade came under pressure during that time as investors questioned the hundreds of billions of dollars tech companies are investing in data centers, and some of the negative sentiment spilled over into quantum computing stocks.

The result was a near-meltdown of IonQ's stock, pushing it down 48% since June.

According to recent reports, it's not all bad news for IonQ. The company has a unique edge in the quantum computing space with its trapped-ion technology helping to reduce error rates (a major problem for quantum computers), and its revenue is climbing.

Sales jumped 336% to nearly $174 million in Q3 2026, and management recently raised its full-year guidance to $510 million, at the midpoint. The tech giant also remarked it has an impressive backlog of $1.2 billion.

IonQ also has $3.7 billion in cash and cash equivalents, so there's no real concern about the company's ability to keep the lights on for the next few years.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/17/26.

There are two simple reasons the stock isn't a bargain: The company remains highly unprofitable, and its shares still look expensive despite the recent drop.

Industry observers note that ionQ's operating losses were $433 million in Q3, and its trailing free cash flow was a negative $689 million. It's worth noting that while the tech giant reported a GAAP (generally accepted accounting principles) net profit of $564 million in Q3 2026, management noted this was due to an $896 million non-cash accounting gain from warrant revaluations rather than operational profitability.

Industry observers note that ionQ CFO Inder Singh said on the latest earnings call that the tech giant is thinking about profitability, but it hasn't publicly estimated when that will occur. "Now that we are moving forward toward potentially being the first quantum company to deliver $1 billion of revenue in the future, it is also time to begin to think about charting out our path to both revenue growth and profitability," Singh said.

It has been revealed that what's more, IonQ stock is still expensive. Even after its sell-off, IonQ's shares have a price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of 29.6, which is far higher than the technology sector's average P/S ratio of 6.5.

That's nowhere near bargain territory for a stock, and given that IonQ won't be profitable anytime soon -- not to mention that it's betting on a very speculative quantum computing market -- investors should proceed with caution before buying this one. If you do pick up some shares right now, it's probably a good idea to add a little to your portfolio over time instead of going headfirst into a large position.

    Arsenal: Kepa; White, Mosquera, Hincapie, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Nwaneri; Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis.

    In a recent development, “When I see the training and how hungry they are for every training drill, that means everybody is ready to compete at the highest level. When you are a player of Arsenal, you compete for every title that is possible. It is not only about the Premier League, it is about all the competitions we are playing for. I see a clear mindset and everything, that everybody is on the same page to win titles here. I saw it from the first training and I think when you train like that in the game, it makes it even better. I came here ready, with my fitness level and I was happy that I could show it here as well. I want to be myself and to show on the pitch all the passion and desire to win because I really like to win games and to give everything.

    “If I give 100% for every game and every duel, I think who does not like this? I think that is the best thing for a football player, and then you will always have the support from the supporters. I am thinking about how to improve and settle as fast as possible in the club, because I have the opportunity to train directly with the team from the beginning of the season, to play pre-season games and then to go to official games. This is a chance to play directly from the beginning and then it is up to me to show the qualities and what I can bring to the team. I am pretty confident I will show it in the next games.”.

    INS:Illan Meslier ⇠ Leeds, FreeChristos Tzolis ⇠ Club Brugge, £34m.

    Piero Hincapie’s move from Bayer Leverkusen was made permanent this summer.

    OUTS:Leandro Trossard ⇢ Besiktas, £18mJakub Kiwior ⇢ Porto, £15m.

    It has been revealed that arsenal are closing in on the signing of Newcastle and Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimaraes in a deal worth £75m. He has been given permission to undergo a medical today and is set to join Arsenal in the coming days. One midfielder coming into Arsenal is set to see another depart as Dane Christian Norgaard closes in on a move to Everton after just one season at Arsenal.

    August 1- Girona 1 Arsenal 4Today- Arsenal vs Real BetisAugust 9- Arsenal vs Borussia DortmundAugust 12- Arsenal vs ComoAugust 16- Arsenal vs Manchester City (Community Shield).

    Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the latest season as they take on Spanish side Real Betis at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin, with this being the first-ever meeting between the two sides. This is the first time Arsenal have played a pre-season game in Dublin since August 2018, when they drew 1-1 with London rivals Chelsea, with Arsenal winning on penalties.

    According to recent reports, arsenal beat Girona 4-1 in their opening game of pre-season, with new signing Christos Tzolis on the scoresheet in his first appearance for the club. After today, Arsenal have three more games, including the Community Shield, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry on opening night of the new season. They are closing in on a deal for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, who is set to become one of Arsenal’s most expensive signings. Mikel Arteta’s side have been dealt a blow ahead of the season with the news that France centre-back William Saliba will miss an extended period due to a back injury. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

    According to recent reports, real Betis, under the management of former Manchester City boss Manuel Pellegrini, finished fifth in La Liga last season and have therefore qualified for this coming season’s Champions League after a 20-year absence from the competition. Pellegrini has led Betis into European competitions for five consecutive seasons, which includes losing the 2025 Europa Conference League final to Chelsea. They have been busy in pre-season action already having played five games up to this point. They have won four of the five, including a 4-0 victory over Lyon, with just one defeat coming against Granada.

    In a recent development, they have a number of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Antony, Giovani Lo Celso, Pablo Fornals and former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin. Real Betis have already played a number of friendlies as they build up to the start of their season, which begins on August 21 when they take on Real Sociedad.

    #27294. Industry News: Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1023 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

    📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1023 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
    • Recent findings suggest that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
    • The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

    Recent findings suggest that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

    The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

    Spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

    Recent findings suggest that the high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

    Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," said Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

    It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he said.

    Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

    "The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone noted.

    He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

    That mentioned, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

    According to recent reports, "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

    While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

    In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, noted Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

    "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she said.

    Sources indicate that the lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, stated Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

    The overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he remarked. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

    Industry observers note that in addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

    The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she said.

    Industry observers note that "It is isolated," she stated. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

    For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

    "We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she said.

    Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

    But there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

    "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin said. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

    Sources indicate that it's also important to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, stated R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

    "With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

    High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo remarked.

    "That's when spreads really widen out," he remarked. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

    Industry News: Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong

    📅 07 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3249 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.
    • Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick.
    • Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

    Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

    Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

    Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

    Stepping up in the big moments! 🐐🧤 pic.twitter.com/r14rF39XpR.

    Unai Emery’s men head home from the Far East to face PSG in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg next week and then have one more pre-season friendly against Borussia Monchengladbach before starting their Premier League campaign at Brighton.

    Possession: Aston Villa 44%-56% Bayern MunichShots: 8-16Shots on target: 3-8Corners: 3-7.

    Bizot nearly has a calamitous moment coming out of his penalty area but gets away with it.

    The final whistle is blown soon after and Bayern hold on to beat Villa 2-1 in Hong Kong. They had looked comfortable when Diaz put them 2-0 up but Villa kept going until the end.

    Victory in the final match of the #AudiFCBTour! 💪🔥 pic.twitter.com/UFhQhme62i.

    The space opens up for Palhinha to shoot from range but Bizot makes a fairly comfortable save down to his right.

    It was all Bayern for 80 minutes of this game but Villa have come to life in the closing stages, with Vincent Kompany’s side now holding on a bit.

    There will be four added minutes.

    Sources indicate that when Diaz scored Bayern’s second goal, Aston Villa were out of this game but it has been all Villa since then. They look the more likely to get a goal.

    According to recent reports, gomes’ free-kick out on the left is parried behind by Neuer for a Villa corner on the right. The corner comes to nothing.

    In a recent development, for 80 minutes, Aston Villa barely looked like scoring but come so close to getting two goals in just a few minutes. Abraham meets a cross from the right and must think he has scored but his header is brilliantly saved by the 40-year-old Neuer.

    Maybe this game is not quite done and dusted yet. A cross from the right picks out Gomes on the edge of the box. The Brazilian takes one touch before toe poking past Neuer and into the Bayern net. Gomes meant that finish and Villa have some hope.

    Abraham should have done better there. He has the space to drive down Villa’s right and has a decision to make; cross the ball to his left and drive forward himself to shoot. He takes a while to make the decision before his attempted cross is intercepted by Ito.

    Boey’s yellow card was his final act of the game as he is replaced by Della Rovere. Boey did seem to be struggling with some cramp.

    Bayern receive their second yellow card of the game as Boey is booked for cynically pulling down Lynch.

    Cash, Maatsen and Buendia have gone off for Aston Villa.

    Double substitution from Bayern as Pavic and Assomo replace Tah and Brown.

    A fantastic goal to put the Germans 2-0 up and it is nothing more than they deserve. Ibrahimovic finds Diaz in space on the left and the Colombian drives at Cash. As he enters the Villa box, Diaz cuts inside onto his preferred right foot and smashes a shot towards goal. It appeared to go right over Bizot, who opts not to put a hand up. The ball crashes off the underside of the bar and goes in. It has been all Bayern in this second half and that goal had been coming.

    Bayern are knocking on the door and come very close to doubling their lead. Diaz’s shot from the edge of the box looks destined to hit the net with Bizot beaten but fortunately for Villa Abraham is on hand on his own goal line to make the block.

    In a recent development, bizot makes another great save. Bayern win a free-kick out on the right after Brown was fouled. Bischoff opts to shoot instead of crossing and nearly beats Bizot at his near post but the Aston Villa keeper gets across to his left to make the save.

    Unai Emery makes a double substitution as Mings and Lynch replace Torres and Guessand. Mings takes the captain’s armband.

    That is a fantastic double save from Bizot, first denying Stanisic and then Ibrahimovic. Both of those shots came through bodies so Bizot did a good job of reacting and making the saves with his legs on both occasions.

    It is safe to say the Bayern fans out in Hong Kong love Diaz, who is cheered every time he touches the ball.

    It has been revealed that vincent Kompany is going to make a triple change as Ito, Diaz and Palhinha come on. Former Liverpool man Diaz received a great ovation from the fans in Hong Kong. Palhinha, who spent last season on loan at Tottenha, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa in this window.

    Industry observers note that should Bayern have been awarded a penalty there? A ball is played in behind the Villa defence into the penalty area and Ibrahimovic appeared to be brought down but the referee waves those appeals away. On first viewing, that appeared to be a penalty.

    Recent findings suggest that just before the hour mark, it is time for some changes from Aston Villa. Abraham and Bogarde come on for Madjo and Kamara. This is Abraham’s first appearance of this pre-season.

    In a recent development, good play from Gomes earns Aston Villa a free-kick not far outside the Bayern penalty area out on the left, in a similar position to the free-kick that Bayern scored from in the first half. Buendia clips in a good ball to the back post, where Guessand looks likely to score but instead misses the ball on the stretch. Should Guessand have done better with that? Probably.

    Brown was starting in his customary left-back position for Bayern in the first half but is now operating out on the right wing.

    Gomes leaves one late on Pavlovic and, had this been a competitive fixture, I suspect that might have been a yellow card.

    Tah is brought down by Gomes and Bayern will have a free-kick out on the right not a million miles outside the Villa penalty area. The delivery though is poor and easily cleared away.

    Bayern have brought Stanisic on at half-time for Laimer. Aston Villa have not made a change at the break.

    We are back under way in Hong Kong.

    Possession: Aston Villa 45%-55% Bayern MunichShots: 4-7Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 1-2.

    The first half in Hong Kong is brought to an end and Bayern take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Kim’s goal.

    There will be one added minute at the end of this first half.

    Sources indicate that aston Villa have struggled to create much going forward and have not really had a genuine goal-scoring opportunity in this first half. Their forward line though will look quite different when they kick off the seaosn than it does today.

    It has been revealed that the German side take the lead in Hong Kong. Bischof’s left-footed delivery from a free-kick out on the left is sublime, whipping it right into the corridor of uncertainty. The quality of delivery means it is quite a simple header for Kim, who makes no mistake with his header into the far corner. Kim might have been offside but obviously there is no VAR in use today. 1-0 Bayern.

    Sources indicate that that is a waste in the end from Bayern. Boey fires a pass in-field into Laimer, who takes a fantastic first touch on the turn inside the Villa half. He drives through the Villa half and at the penalty area but his pass outside looking for Cardozo is poor and overhit, with the ball rolling out for a goal kick. Laimer will be annoyed at himself having done all the hard work and then failed to execute the easy part.

    In a recent development, bischof eyes one up from range and tries to pick out the top corner. Bizot is routed to his spot and is hoping the shot goes wide. Bischof’s effort is always curling wide, much to Bizot’s relief.

    The first booking of the game goes the way of Bayern Munich. Guessand drives forward into the Bayern half and is brought down by a cynical foul from Cardozo. You were half expecting Cardozo to perhaps escape without a booking with it being a pre-season friendly but he does not. It was the right call to book him.

    It has been revealed that that was lovely from Pavlovic. The German midfielder highlights good feet to beat Gomes before getting his shot away from a central position just outside the box. He forces Bizot into a decent save but one he should be making.

    Recent findings suggest that bayern force Villa into an error and win themselves a corner as a result out on the left. It is delivered into a dangerous area at the front post but Villa do a good job of handling it and clearing their lines.

    Recent findings suggest that bayern Munich have made two signings this summer; Brown from Bundesliga rivals Frankfurt and Saibari from PSV. Brown is starting at left-back for Bayern today with Saibari not involved as he closes in on a return from a knock picked up at the World Cup with Morocco. Brown feels like such a Bayern signing, nabbing a good player from a Bundesliga rival.

    Aston Villa have made four signings so far this summer but just one is in their starting XI today in the form of Gomes, who joined from Midlands rivals Wolves this summer. Young Swiss midfielder Manzambi has joined from Freiburg but is at the moment out injured. Garnacho picked up a knock and Cisse, who has arrived from LASK, is not involved for Villa today.

    According to recent reports, the ball is played in behind the Aston Villa defence to pick out the run of Binder. On the edge of the Villa box, Binder gets the first touch but Lindelof is calm in defence and heads back to his keeper Bizot.

    Moments later, Gomes is dispossessed inside his own half and Ibrahimovic has a shot from just outside the box but drags it wide of the far post.

    Industry observers note that good work from 17-year-old Madjo down Aston Villa’s left wins them their first corner of the game. Buendia’s inswinger is headed away too easily at the near post. Aston Villa have seen their former set-piece coach Austin MacPhee nabbed this summer by Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea.

    The referee is allowing the game to flow and thus not blowing for soft fouls.

    Industry observers note that the first chance of the game falls to Bayern Munich. Brown’s cross from the left is headed by Maatsen straight to Ibrahimovic on the edge of the box. Ibrahimovic, not any relation to Zlatan, takes the shot on first time but it is blocked by Maatsen, who makes up for that poor header with the block. The ball goes behind for a corner, which comes to nothing.

    Sources indicate that interestingly, there are only eight outfield substitutions on the Aston Villa bench for this game, with the likes of Garnacho and McGinn picking up knocks the other day. It appears then that at least a couple of Villa outfield players will have to play the full 90.

    In a recent development, both sides emerge from the tunnel, Aston Villa led out by Matty Cash and Bayern Munich by Manuel Neuer, and we are closing in on kick-off in Hong Kong. A group of delegates shake the hands of both starting XIs.

    Chelsea and Juventus played in this stadium the other night and it is safe to say that the pitch does not look in the best state ahead of kick-off today. It looks like it will continue to rip up and the last thing the two managers will want is to pick up any serious injuries.

    Currently, before the two sides emerge, the crowd in Hong Kong are being treated to some pre-match dancing and entertainment, which includes people dressed as pandas and sharks dancing. Would the Premier League ever take inspiration and have dancing pandas before kick-off?

    Aston Villa: Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen, Kamara, Joao Gomes, Hemmings, Buendia, Guessand, Madjo.Substitutes: Wright, Asemota, Mings, Abraham, Nedejkovic, Bogarde, Rowe, Burrowes, Carroll, Lynch.

    Bayern Munich: Neuer, Kim, Tah, Brown, Boey, Laimer, Bischof, Pavlovic, Ibrahimovic, Binder, Cardozo. Substitutes: Ulrich, Podar-Stiube, Urbig, Kimmich, Luis Díaz, Palhinha, Ito, Chávez, Pavic, Bara, Manuba, Stanisic, Della Rovere, Assomo.

    The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return to training after their World Cup exploits and Aston Villa are also without captain John McGinn and new signing Alejandro Garnacho, who picked up knocks in their win over BG Pathum the other day.

    Industry observers note that aston Villa have already sold Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers this summer, with Lucas Digne on the verge of a move to PSG, but could another starter be on the way out of Villa Park? England defender Ezri Konsa has been linked with moves to the likes of Arsenal and Liverpool but will Unai Emery be able to keep hold of the 28-year-old?

    The atmosphere is building with our fans in Hong Kong! 🔴⚪️#AudiFCBTour pic.twitter.com/m4fFXAWxGb.

    INS:Johan Manzambi ⇠ Freiburg, £50mJoao Gomes ⇠ Wolves, £34mAlejandro Garnacho ⇠ Chelsea, LoanModou Keba Cisse ⇠ LASK, £5m.

    OUTS:Youri Tielemans ⇢ Manchester United, £36mDonyell Malen ⇢ Roma, £20mMorgan Rogers ⇢ Chelsea, £117mLewis Dobbin ⇢ Southampton, £10mEnzo Barrenechea ⇢ Benfica, £10.

    In a recent development, it has been a big summer of change at Aston Villa already and there could be more changes before the end of the window. Left-back Lucas Digne is set to move to PSG and is set to be replaced by Atlético Madrid’s Matteo Ruggeri. Joao Palhinha, who is on the bench for Bayern Munich today, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa.

    “Aston Villa are a top side with a very good coach. They have a large squad and will field plenty of talent. They have already played more friendlies than us, but for us it is a good challenge. It is a match in which we will learn a lot about our team’s fitness. It will be a good match for us.”.

    Sources indicate that “It is difficult to improve; after all, it is not just about the trophies we have won, but also about the number of goals and matches we have won. It is possible, but difficult. Right now, I would say our aim is to win the Champions League; there is no doubt about that. And throughout the season, I will be saying that we need to focus on the next match. To achieve that; to win the Bundesliga, the cup and the Champions League, we need the whole squad to be fit and healthy. We need to make good use of them and improve the squad. We have already done that, but hopefully it will help us achieve our goals.”.

    Your Aston Villa team to face Bayern Munich in Hong Kong 👊 pic.twitter.com/VxyopTRMFp.

    Here's how we line up to face Aston Villa 🔴𝗪𝗔𝗧𝗖𝗛 𝗟𝗜𝗩𝗘! From 13:55 👉 https://t.co/gFwG0Y99m8#AudiFCBTour pic.twitter.com/JmkEytIjIF.

    special, one-off lettering and numbering for our clash with Bayern Munich in Hong Kong ✨ pic.twitter.com/7v3cEk5vec.

    July 21- Walsall 0 Aston Villa 5July 25- Porto 2 Aston Villa 1July 28- Aston Villa 2 Real Sociedad 4August 1- Indonesia All Stars 1 Aston Villa 3August 4- BG Pathum 1 Aston Villa 3Today- Aston Villa vs Bayern MunichAugust 12- PSG vs Aston Villa (Uefa Super Cup)August 15- Borussia Monchengladbach vs Aston Villa.

    Aston Villa’s preparations for the fresh season continue out in Hong Kong as they take on Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich at the Kai Tak Stadium. These sides have met twice before; Aston Villa beat Bayern 1-0 to win the European Cup in 1981/82 before then meeting in the Champions League group stages during the 2024/25 season, with Jhon Duran’s long-range screamer giving Aston Villa a 1-0 win at Villa Park.

    After losing two of their first three pre-season friendlies, Aston Villa have won their first two games on Asian soil and this game marks the end of their tour of the Far East. It has been a summer of significant change at Aston Villa thus far with some key members of their squad departing and some new faces arriving. Youri Tielemans has departed after Manchester United triggered his release clause and they then sold Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for a British transfer record £117m. Unai Emery’s side have brought in 20-year-old Swiss midfielder Johan Manzambi, Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes and Alejandro Garnacho, with the deal for Garnacho being an initial loan. Manzambi is currently on the sidelines due to a knee injury.

    Unai Emery’s side were dealt a blow during the World Cup as Belgian midfielder Amadou Onana picked up a serious knee injury. They were though boosted by the return of Boubacar Kamara after seven months out as he scored in the 3-1 friendly victory over BG Parthum. As one midfielder returned from injury in that game, another picked up a fresh injury as John McGinn suffered a knock to his knee. The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return after their world Cup exploits. They begin their Premier League campaign with an away game on the south coast against Brighton on August 23 but will be involved in the Uefa Super Cup against PSG next week having lifted the Europa League last season.

    Recent findings suggest that bayern Munich head into this season looking to win a third straight Bundesliga title and have won two of their three friendlies, losing once. They have added Moroccan attacker Ismael Saibari from PSV and German left-back Nathaniel Brown from Bundesliga rivals Eintracht Frankfurt to their ranks this summer.     Hawks' CJ McCollum out at least 4 weeks with calf strain, putting rookie Kingston Flemings in the spotlight

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (487 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, atlanta Hawks guard CJ McCollum has a left calf strain and will be sidelined for at least four weeks.
    • McCollum sustained the injury in Sunday's win over the Milwaukee Bucks.
    • Recent findings suggest that through 14 games, McCollum is averaging 14.5 points, 3.9 assists, 3.1 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game while shooting 43.3% from the floor and 35.2% from 3.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, atlanta Hawks guard CJ McCollum has a left calf strain and will be sidelined for at least four weeks. The Hawks revealed the injury update on Tuesday.

    McCollum sustained the injury in Sunday's win over the Milwaukee Bucks. Imaging has since revealed the calf strain. He'll be reevaluated in four weeks, per the Hawks.

    Recent findings suggest that through 14 games, McCollum is averaging 14.5 points, 3.9 assists, 3.1 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game while shooting 43.3% from the floor and 35.2% from 3. The Hawks enter Tuesday at 8-6, tied with the Miami Heat for the fourth-best record in the Eastern Conference.

    The injury is a blow for the Hawks as they lose a key playmaker and their veteran voice on the court.

    McCollum, 35, began the season as Atlanta's starting point guard. But he gave way to rookie Kingston Flemings in the starting unit, recently telling the NBA on Prime that he approached head coach Quin Snyder about making the lineup change.

    "I didn't like the way we were playing as a unit, as a starting unit," McCollum said. "I think we were a little sluggish. I think we were lackluster from a ball movement standpoint.

    "I think we were stagnant, and we have a lot of guys that can create and make plays. And I think for Kingston, he's a guy who gets downhill. He's got tremendous speed. He's learning and growing. And I think it gives him a chance to kind of develop, for us as a franchise and for us as an organization. ….

    "The way I play, I can get to it off the bench, I can get to it as a starter. I'm mature enough to be able to handle different roles, different minutes.".

    According to recent reports, with McCollum sidelined, the keys to the offense will belong to Flemings, whom the Hawks selected with the No. 8 pick in June's draft out of Houston. In 12 games including five starts, Flemings is averaging 7.8 points, 4.1 assists, 2.5 rebounds and 0.7 steals in 21.5 minutes per game.

    In a recent development, flemings' shooting efficiency has stood out, especially for a rookie. He's shooting 51.4% from the field and 42.9% on 1.8 3-point attempts per game. He's done so in limited playing time as McCollum has continued to play heavy minutes off the bench.

    Recent findings suggest that flemings has been day-to-day with back tightness, but was reportedly able to practice on Tuesday. He projects to have an opportunity to build on his success with increased volume and playing time in McCollum's absence.

    The Hawks also declared Tuesday that second-year backup forward Asa Newell will miss at least four months with a plantar plate tear in his left great toe that required surgery. Newell was averaging 3.6 points and 2.6 rebounds in 11 minutes per game in five appearances this season.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that uncertainty in the Middle East, elevated Treasury yields and fears about an AI bubble continue to keep global markets on edge.
    • However, the vast universe of dividend stocks can make selection challenging.
    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that uncertainty in the Middle East, elevated Treasury yields and fears about an AI bubble continue to keep global markets on edge. Given this volatile backdrop, investors seeking stable income can consider enhancing their portfolios by adding dividend-paying stocks.

    However, the vast universe of dividend stocks can make selection challenging. Tracking the ratings of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend stocks, as their recommendations are backed by in-depth research.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Recent findings suggest that chord Energy is an independent exploration and production organization with long-lived assets primarily in the Williston Basin. With a quarterly base dividend of $1.30 per share, CHRD offers a dividend yield of 3.67%.

    In a research note on third-quarter expectations, RBC Capital analyst Scott Hanold reiterated a buy rating on CHRD stock with a price target of $175. "We model production near the top of guidance and continue to see strong performance from fresh wells and base production," stated Hanold.

    In a recent development, specifically, the five-star analyst expects Q3 2026 production at 283 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day, or Mboe/d, in line with the Street's consensus and near the high end of the 278 to 284 Mboe/d guidance. Hanold mentioned his Q3 2026 earnings per share estimate increased to $5.29 due to lower non-cash depreciation, depletion and amortization.

    According to recent reports, meanwhile, cash flow per share estimate moved lower to $13.59 to reflect Hanold's upgrade based on the current backdrop and commodity mark-to-market. He expects Chord Energy to report capital spending of $375 million for Q3 2026, slightly above the Street's estimate of $369 million.

    In a recent development, overall, Hanold remains bullish on CHRD, given its best-in-class balance sheet. He expects a free cash flow payout of 80% in the third quarter, with the possibility of an upside. Hanold expects investors to focus on management commentary on 2027 capital plans, Williston M&A opportunities, and long-term performance of 4-mile wells.

    Hanold ranks No. 310 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 14.9%. See Chord Energy KPIs on TipRanks.

    Williams, an energy infrastructure company that delivers natural gas, is the next dividend pick. The company recently completed the $5.5 billion acquisition of Momentum Midstream, which will expand its natural gas infrastructure in the Haynesville to meet growing Gulf Coast LNG, power and industrial demand. At a quarterly dividend of $0.5250 per share, Williams offers a yield of 2.89%.

    Sources indicate that in her latest research note, RBC Capital analyst Elvira Scotto reiterated a buy rating on Williams stock with a price target of $87. Ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, the analyst said that she expects WMB to announce strong quarterly performance.

    Scotto raised her estimates to reflect insights from the quarterly catch-up call, the completion of the Momentum Midstream acquisition, and mark-to-market quarter-to-date commodity prices. She expects WMB to report Q3 2026 adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $2,036 million, which is modestly above the Street's consensus estimate.

    Furthermore, Scotto expects Williams' Transmission, Power & Gulf segment to increase quarter-over-quarter, driven by the startup of the Socrates power project and favorable natural gas liquids, or NGL, margins.

    Scotto noted that WMB stock has underperformed due to backlash related to data centers and investor anticipation of another Power Innovation project. She expects the organization to announce at least one more project before the end of this year, potentially with a fresh customer and a contract duration of 15 to 20 years, which would be a positive catalyst for the stock.

    Recent findings suggest that scotto ranks No. 175 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been profitable 67% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.2%. See Williams Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Recent findings suggest that EOG Resources, a crude oil and natural gas exploration and production company, will hold its third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 6. At a quarterly dividend of $1.02 per share, EOG offers a dividend yield of 2.75%.

    Heading into Q3 earnings, Jefferies analyst Lloyd Byrne reiterated a buy rating on EOG Resources stock and increased his price target to $185 from $175. The analyst expects the company's Q3 cash flow per share to exceed the Street's consensus by 13%, driven by better-than-expected production.

    Byrne expects crude oil production, excluding the UAE, to reach 551 Mboe/d, which is at the high end of guidance (546-551 Mboe/d) and above the Street's projection of 548 Mboe/d, driven by continued growth in the Utica.

    Sources indicate that furthermore, Byrne expects cash operating expenses to come in at $10.27 per barrel of oil equivalent, below the midpoint of guidance of $10.05 to $11.35, helped by lower lease operating expenses. Overall, the analyst expects EOG to deliver free cash flow of $2.65 billion, supporting another quarter of buybacks near the minimum 70% shareholder return threshold and implying about $1.5 billion in share repurchases.

    "As a first indication of the '27 plan, we expect EOG will message another year of mid-single-digit (~3.5%) growth on a flat capital budget (~$6.55bn), which is above the Street modeling 1% oil growth at $6.6bn," said Byrne.

    Recent findings suggest that byrne ranks No. 303 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 58% of the time, delivering an average return of 18.5%. See EOG Resources Statistics on TipRanks.

    #27266. Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan

    📅 08 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 16m • 📚 Deep Dive (3190 w)
