    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan

    📅 08 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3190 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday.
    • The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.
    • The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

    The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

    The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

    In a recent development, just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

    MOISÉS CAICEDO THAT IS INCREDIBLE 🤯 pic.twitter.com/C6CEcUG1sE.

    Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

    Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

    Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

    AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

    In a recent development, chelsea managed to lure Austin MacPhee to take care of their set-pieces and today Chelsea scored two goals from corners. Here is a snippet of Mike McGrath’s piece on MacPhee’s arrival at Chelsea:.

    He is among the new breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

    It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

    Chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the newly introduced season.

    AC Milan will play Manchester United next weekend and then kick off their Serie A campaign against Torino.

    Possession: Chelsea 50%-50% AC MilanShots: 18-5Shots on target: 8-0Corners: 7-2.

    The final whistle is blown in Jakarta and Chelsea have cruised to a 3-0 win over AC Milan. Goals from Caicedo and a double from Pedro either side of half-time have led Xabi Alonso’s side to the victory. They have one more game out in the Far East before returning home to the UK.

    According to recent reports, what a performance! 👏 pic.twitter.com/GcUZXwXbRj.

    Sources indicate that ramos is picked out after making a run into the Chelsea box and is denied by Sanchez. However, the offside flag has gone up anyway against Ramos. AC Milan have barely threatened the Chelsea goal in this second half.

    A late change for Chelsea as Sarr replaces Fofana.

    There will be five added minutes.

    Chelsea are seeking their fourth goal as Quenda strikes a shot powerfully from just outside the box but it goes narrowly wide. Xabi Alonso’s side have dominated this second half.

    Estevao has the chance to score moments after coming on after good work from the Brazilian down Chelsea’s right but is denied by a good save from Torriani.

    Chelsea make a triple changes as Estevao, Mudryk and Watson come on. Mudryk made his return after his doping ban against Juventus during the week.

    Chelsea hit the frame of the goal once more. Jackson gets the better of Vladimirov down Chelsea’s left and moves into the AC Milan penalty area. Jackson opens up his body as if he is going to curl his shot into the far corner but instead shoots towards the near corner, with his effort coming off the post.

    Ricci goes for an audacious strike with the outside of his right foot from outside the box but his effort misses the target.

    Palmer was deep in conversation with his boss Alonso during that water break.

    Chelsea made a substitution during that break as Anselmino comes on for Hato. Thus far, Chelsea have made three changes in this game and Alonso did confirm before the game that some players should be able to go the full 90 this far into pre-season.

    Time for the second half water break.

    Sources indicate that chelsea hit the post. Quenda receives the ball on the right side of the penalty area and quickly moves the ball onto his right foot. The 19-year-old then smashes a shot towards goal and the ball flies into the outside of the post. Quenda struck that with some venom.

    Palmer has a chance to get Chelsea’s fourth from the left side of the box but AC Milan keeper Torriani makes the save down to his left.

    AC Milan have offered very little going forward since the break and Sanchez has not been troubled in the Chelsea goal.

    Recent findings suggest that AC Milan have a good chance to get a goal back. Musah finds space on the right side of the box and cuts it back towards the penalty spot. He picks out Nkunku but the former Chelsea man wastes the opportunity.

    Palestra is found with a cross from the right to the far post. Palestra takes a touch but his shot goes into the side netting.

    Ruben Amorim is demanding a free-kick just outside the Chelsea box but the referee does not agree. Replays show that AC Milan probably should have been given the free-kick as it was a foul by Fofana on Ramos. Both players went down but are back to their feet.

    Xabi Alonso is going to make his first two changes of the game as Jackson and Quenda replace Welbeck and Neto.

    It has been revealed that chelsea have their third and their upcoming set-piece coach Austin MacPhee will be delighted with that one. Lavia plays a flat delivery from a corner out on the left to Caicedo on the edge of the box. Caicedo hits it first time on the volley with the outside of his right foot and picks out the bottom right corner with perfection.

    It has been revealed that chelsea go 2-0 up not even a minute into the second half. Neto, on the right side of the box, cuts onto his preferred left foot and crosses to the far post. Pedro gets on the end of it and, despite the Milan keeper getting a touch on the shot, the ball ends up in the far corner.

    AC Milan have made a raft of changes at the break, which includes their newly introduced record signing Ramos, who has joined from PSG this summer. Former Chelsea man Nkunku is also on. Milan were back out from the dressing rooms a fair bit earlier than Chelsea were. It is rather farcical how long Chelsea took to re-emerge for the second half and they just saunter out as if nothing is up. Why on earth did the officials just allow Chelsea to take over 20 minutes for half-time?

    Nearly 25 minutes after the first half concluded, we are finally back under way in Jakarta.

    Possession: Chelsea 58%-42% AC MilanShots: 6-4Shots on target: 3-0Corners: 4-2.

    The first half in Jakarta is brought an end and Chelsea take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Pedro’s goal on the stroke of half-time.

    According to recent reports, 90 seconds into added time at the end of this first half, we have the first goal in Jakarta. Caicedo’s delivery from the right picks out Pedro, who has a free header inside the six-yard box and makes no mistake, picking out the corner. Pedro really should not have been afforded so much space in the six-yard box.

    Palestra makes a run in behind the AC Milan defence and is found but De Winter gets back to put it behind for a corner...

    Due to the water break, there will be three additional minutes at the end of this first half.

    It has been revealed that the first booking of the game goes the way of AC Milan as Pavlovic clears out Palestra. A deserved booking.

    Industry observers note that neto and Pedro exchange a good one-two down Chelsea’s right to put the former racing down the right wing. Neto then tries to find Welbeck in the centre of the box but it is just behind him.

    Industry observers note that then, moments later, Pedro spurns a great chance for Chelsea. Palestra’s cross from the left is just out of Palmer’s reach but falls straight to Pedro, who blazes over from 12 yards out. He was leaning back and should really be hitting the target.

    Recent findings suggest that the space opens up for Palmer to take on a shot from range but his effort is blocked by De Winter. Palmer has not managed to have that much of an effect on this game thus far.

    In a recent development, pavlovic drives forward from his defensive position through the Chelsea half. He gets all the way to the Chelsea box before shooting but he looked to lack conviction, firing off target.

    We will pause for a drinks break, which unfortunately we became accustomed to during the World Cup. Palmer takes the chance to take a seat on the bench whilst taking on some fluids.

    Neto takes a first-time shot from outside the box and looks to curl it into the far corner, forcing Torriani into a decent save diving down to his right.

    That is good one-vs-one defending from Achemapong. Estupinan plays the ball into the path of Leao, who drives through the Chelsea half down AC Milan’s left. As Leao approaches the Chelsea box, Leao attempts to push it past Acheampong but the young Chelsea defender times his sliding challenge to perfection and puts it behind for a corner. Sanchez punches it out to the edge of the box, where Comotto takes it on his chest before volleying towards goal. The ball goes behind for another corner, which Chelsea just about scramble away.

    According to recent reports, chelsea hit the post. Palestra drives forward for Chelsea down their left before the ball falls to Welbeck on the left side of the box. Welbeck’s effort hits the outside of the post. AC Milan keeper Torriani appeared though to always have it covered.

    Sources indicate that chelsea gift the ball away inside their own half and Leao drives forward. The Portuguese forward moves into the Chelsea penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is blocked.

    Industry observers note that A big, big chance for Chelsea to take the lead. A long ball is played forward in behind the AC Milan defence and Pedro gets the better of De Winter inside the Milan penalty area. It is then a one-on-one chance with Torriani but Pedro hits it straight at the Milan goalkeeper. Torriani should have come to claim that long ball and then Pedro should probably have buried that opportunity.

    Chelsea win their third corner of the game as Palmer’s cross from the right takes a couple of deflections off AC Milan defender. Captain Caicedo has trotted over to take it out on the left. He sends it into a good area but a foul on the AC Milan keeper Torriani is given against Pedro.

    It has been revealed that neto clips a free-kick into the AC Milan penalty area, which is chested down by Pedro. The Brazilian holds the ball up well inside the box before winning a corner. Chelsea play it short and Palmer crosses to the back post, where Palestra wins Chelsea another corner, this time out on the left.

    Caicedo’s inswinging delivery is headed away at the front post.

    Palestra, who has joined Chelsea this summer from Atalanta, is proving his versatility today; he has mostly operated for Chelsea at right-back so far this pre-season but he is starting at left-back in this game.

    Camarda is played in behind the Chelsea defence and tries to get the better of Fofana inside the Chelsea penalty area but the ball just runs out of play across the byline before Camarda can square the ball.

    We are under way in Jakarta, Indonesia, in Chelsea’s penultimate game over in the Far East. Before the game started, a huge AC Milan tifo was unveiled at one end of the ground.

    It is 7pm in Jakarta yet the temperature is still up at 29 degrees with the humidity at nearly 70%. These conditions will be a proper test for both sides.

    The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

    The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

    According to recent reports, yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

    INS:Marco Palestra ⇠ Atalanta, £42mGeovany Quenda ⇠ Sporting, £42mMorgan Rogers ⇠ Aston Villa, £117mMaxence Lacroix ⇠ Crystal Palace, £51mDanny Welbeck ⇠ Brighton, UndisclosedJordan Henderson ⇠ Brentford, FreeValentin Barco ⇠ Strasbourg, Undisclosed.

    OUTS:Andrey Santos ⇢ Manchester United, £50mMarc Cucurella ⇢ Real Madrid, £50mTyrique George ⇢ Everton, £24mAlejandro Garnacho ⇢ Aston Villa, Loan.

    Chelsea are on the verge of making yet another signing with Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria close to securing a move to Stamford Bridge.

    Chelsea: Sanchez; Palestra, Acheampong, Fofana, Hato; Palmer, Caicedo, Lavia, Neto; Welbeck, Joao Pedro.Substitutes: Sharman-Lowe, Penders, Sarr, Anselmino, Tosin, Subuloye, Essugo, Nicoll-Jazuli, Watson, Walsh, Satpayev, Quenda, Gittens, Estevao, Mudryk, Jackson, Delap.

    According to recent reports, AC Milan: Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Pavlovic; Chukwueze, Modric, Comotto, Estupinan; Loftus-Cheek, Leao; Camarda.Substitutes: Ricci, G. Ramos, Diawara, Nkunku, Fofana, Tomori, Athekame, Odogu, Jashari, Bartesaghi, Vladimirov, Pittarella, Gabbia, Saelemakers, Cisse, Musah.

    Recent findings suggest that the English forward joined Chelsea from Borussia Dortmund last summer for just under £50m. He struggled to make an impact last season in his first year at Chelsea, failing to register a goal in the Premier League or Champions League but did spend most of the second half of last season on the sidelines due to an injury. Gittens, who is on the bench for Chelsea today, has been speaking this week to CFC+:.

    Sources indicate that “I am feeling, I would say, more confident now, in my body as well. The injury that happened [impacted my first season], but I am feeling better every day. I am trying to improve every day to be the best version of myself. It has been good to be back with the boys. I am really enjoying it right now and it has been really good to be part of this team.”.

    Have a great day, Jamie. 🥳 pic.twitter.com/QeX83XrXAM.

    In Chelsea’s defeat to Juventus in midweek, Ukrainian forward Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 after a long doping ban was resolved. You can read all about that game right here. Mudryk is on the bench for Chelsea today.

    Industry observers note that our line-up to face AC Milan! pic.twitter.com/MK2hd0c708.

    July 28- Western Sydney Wanderers 4 Chelsea 6August 1- Chelsea 1 Tottenham 2August 5- Chelsea 0 Juventus 1Today- Chelsea vs AC MilanAugust 9- Johor Darul Ta’z vs ChelseaAugust 15- Chelsea vs Real Sociedad.

    Current Chelsea defender Tosin Adarabioyo has been catching up with former Chelsea men Ruben Loftus-Cheek, who starts for AC Milan today, and Fikayo Tomori.

    The team news is in from Jakarta! 🗞️ pic.twitter.com/BRBjmlgwz8.

    Industry observers note that the atmosphere is building. 🇮🇩📈 pic.twitter.com/fhXfDVAf6s.

    Recent findings suggest that chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

    Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

    According to recent reports, “We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so important to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”.

    It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

    AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

    📅 18 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (933 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Top Wall Street analysts are bullish on the growth potential of these 3 stocks

    📅 18 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (933 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.
    • Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.
    • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.

    Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Sources indicate that health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The company also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround plan.

    Sources indicate that following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," said Wright.

    The five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the organization's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

    In a recent development, furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the company's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

    Wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.

    In a recent development, wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the firm's AI strategy when it announces its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

    Heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

    According to recent reports, specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active customers in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

    "Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," said the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

    While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently introduced Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the firm's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

    According to recent reports, morris ranks No. 629 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Meta Platforms KPIs on TipRanks.

    In a recent development, next is semiconductor manufacturer Marvell Technology. Earlier this month, Marvell held its Investor Day, where it raised its total addressable market estimate to $400 billion by 2030, reflecting solid AI-led demand tailwinds.

    After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

    The five-star analyst remarked that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.

    While XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the organization raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.

    In a recent development, svanberg said that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. Management said that it met with suppliers ahead of Investor Day to share its five-year goals and received commitments to support these targets. The analyst believes that Marvell's supply chain commitments give it a competitive edge over rivals as customers seek reliable partners for large-scale infrastructure buildouts.

    Svanberg ranks No. 91 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 58% of the time, delivering an average return of 31.8%. See Marvell Technology Statistics on TipRanks.

    #27244. Industry News: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount

    📅 08 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2613 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount

    📅 08 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2613 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.
    • Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.
    • The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

    Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

    The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

    But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

    “He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

    “We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”.

    Post-match video footage indicated Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

    Michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl.

    United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

    Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

    United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

    United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

    According to recent reports, “It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”.

    In a recent development, “It’s good for me. I enjoyed it. We need to build fitness, we have a major season ahead.”.

    “It’s a good game PSG are tough to beat and we got a draw and now think about the next game [against Leeds in Dublin].”.

    It has been revealed that “We have two more games against Leeds a and Milan. We need to have significant season and hope to win a trophy.”.

    All over in Gothenburg and it’s been a good match for Michael Carrick’s team. They looked sharper and quicker than their win over Atletico Madrid last week (what the manager wanted) and things are moving in the right direction. Two things to worry about, however, were the early exits of Mason Mount and Tom Heaton with injuries. They’ll especially hope the Mount knock isn’t anything mid or long term.

    Nearly done and it’s been a good run out for United. They’ve looked the better, sharper side and, if anything, deserve to win. In mitigation, this is United fourth pre-season game to PSG’s second...

    Industry observers note that fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

    Two chances for United in quick succession. A lovely ball from the middle of the park by Zirkzee finds Dalot on the right. He chips the ball to the back post where one of the Fletchers (sorry, I am not sure which) heads for goal. His attempt is blocked and the ball, ultimately, falls at the feet of Lacey whose shot is blazed high over the bar.

    There have been plenty of good things for Carrick to take from this match. The passing, while not of the standard of a cut-and-thrust Premier League match, has been good for the time of year, and there have been enough flashes of brilliance/class/invention etc to suggest that pre-season is moving in the right direction.

    Recent findings suggest that lovely bit of play by United. A great pass with the outside of the boot from the inside-left channel by Tielemans finds Fernandes who plays a sidefooted shot that goes just wide.

    Tielemans’s first bit of brilliance from the Belgian there.

    Industry observers note that both sides losing possession a fair bit at the moment. Strong pre-season vibes right now.

    It has been revealed that maguire has had a good game. He’s played a number of long passes from the back and looked assured. This time he’s up in the PSG half and decides to have a pop - his shot testing Safanov, who saves well.

    Had there been VAR Safanov might have had something to answer for...he may have beaten Zirkzee to the ball but he flew in the air and jurt the United man in the process.

    Anwway, there’s no VAR (hurrah, for those of you who consider it a modern-day evil) and it doesn’t matter.

    Chance for United to go ahead and it comes from two things. (i) A long, hopeful ball from Fernandes that looks for Zirkzee (ii) Safanov rushing off his line and into no-man’s land. The ball comes loose and Jack Fletcher, instead of having a go at goal, with the keeper on the ground and out of the game, passes to Lacey whose shot is wide.

    Recent findings suggest that tyler Fletcher loses the ball near the United half and it, ultimately, results in a PSG corner. From the set piece United defend well and snuff out all hint of danger.

    PSG seeing more of the ball at the moment. They work the ball to the right and Amass brings down Mbaye.

    From the resulting free-kick, in the final third, the French side whip in the ball but Mee is up ot the challenge and come to collect well.

    Santos, Mbeumo, Shaw, Amad, Lacey are off.

    Fernandes, Jack Feltcher, Zirkzee and Amass are on.

    And it’s a debut for Tielemans.

    Sources indicate that A raft of changes for PSG sees Marquinhos and João Neves, among others, come on. More like it, in terms of first-team ‘names’, on the pitch for the European Cup champions.

    United on top in this half, as they were in the first.

    The paces quickens and the game is much better for it. Mbuemo drives toward the PSG box, he cuts inside from the right before unleashing a shot that is bound for the back of the net before a fine one-handed save by Safanov. Credit, too, for Maguire whose long ball from the back found Mbuemo brilliantly. Promising...

    According to recent reports, lacey tries to play in Dorgu on the left but he’s asking too much of his team-mate. Wonder when the expected raft of changes will take place?

    According to recent reports, slow start to the second half. This is very much pre-season-friendly pace.

    It has been revealed that having seen Mount limp off in the first half, there’s more worry at the start of the second and Heaton is force off with what looks like a hamstrung injury. He dashed off his line to clear a ball and in doing so has tweaked something. Mee replaces him.

    Back under way Gothenburg - there have been a number of changes and will bring them to you once I’ve worked out who has come on and who they’ve replaced.

    A world record that still stands...(this was back in 1995).

    And that is it for the first 45 minutes. PSG took the early lead, but from that moment on United have been the better side and deservedly are level through Mbueno’s goal.

    There will be one minute of added time at the end of what has been a good first half for Man Utd.

    Amad has a go from outside the box forcing the save from Safanov. He’s such a live wire and one of the best in his position in the top flight. Him or Antony? No contest, strange it took United a while to work that one out.

    Yet more good work from the underrated Amad. He again closes down well on the right before winning back possession and cutting the ball back for Lacey. To think he was starring for Sunderland in the Championship while Antony was starting for United...

    United have been the better side since conceding earlier and, as if to illustrate my point, as I typed that an Mbuemo free-kick is well saved by Safanov. That was heading for the top-right bin.

    Recent findings suggest that great work on the left by Dorgu and Shaw ends with the latter chipping the ball to the back post where Amad is lurking with intent. The Ivorian looks to head the ball home, but before he can get anything on it it looks as though he’s pushed in the back. United players are sure it’s a penalty but, more importantly, the referee doesn’t.

    Amad does brilliantly, winning the ball off Koukaba in the final third, from there he scampers toward the box before playing in Mbuemo who takes one touch before firing in a shot into the bottom right corner of the net.

    Sources indicate that free-kick for PSG on the right, near the final third. The ball comes in and it’s straight into the arms of Heaton in the United goal.

    Kvaratskhelia, not seen much of him so far, runs into the box, but Amad does well to usher him back out.

    The match is pedestrian at the moment, but as I type that, Dorgu, yep, him again, drives down the left and puts in a good cross that is well intercepted by Safanov in the PSG goal.

    Sources indicate that united continue to see more of the ball, Dorgu’s seeing more of it than most. But, no chances really fashioned, still, plenty of time to go.

    Worry for United having to sub off Mount. It looks as though he took a knock to a foot and Carrick and co will hope it’s not a long-term injury. Mount, who’s had a good pre-season, has been replaced by Fletcher, son of Darren.

    Industry observers note that foul on Mazraoui results in two things. The Mount has to come off, and, United have a free-kick on the edge of the PSG area.

    From the set-piece Mbuemo has a go and it’s a regulation save from Safonov in the PSG goal.

    Industry observers note that heaven loses possession in the middle of the park and from there it’s like the parting of the Red Sea as PSG have a three-on-one. Mbaye gets the shot in on goal but Andrey Santos covers back brilliantly and does enough to get something on the ball. He’s started both this match and pre-season well.

    United are looking half decent on the ball. They’re passing it well and not afraid to switch things around.

    Recent findings suggest that A lovely long ball from Maguire finds Dorgo whose lovely first touch takes him into the box before a cut back is intercepted by a PSG man. Promising signs though for Carrick’s men.

    Industry observers note that united seeing more of the ball at the moment. They’re being patient but cannot fashion an opening and the ball is worked all the way back to Heaton in goal.

    Needless to say this is being played at a slowish pace...no blood-and-guts challenges being put in.

    It has been revealed that good work down the right sees Amad plays in Shay Lacey who crosses into the box. The ball find shte head of Mbuemo and the ball sails over the bar. Better from United.

    United started slowly against Atletico and they’ve done the same here.

    Bright start to say the least from the French side. They work the ball left and it’s an easy cross from Dro Fernandez for Mbaye to tap home for the very early lead.

    According to recent reports, they’re under way in Sweden. United are in their upcoming vibrant red kit and PSG in their blue, red and white kit. Big fan of the French side’s kit, it harks back to the kit they had in the 1990s when the likes of George Weah and David Ginola were entertaining in the capital of France.

    A reminder of how they line up.

    Man Utd: Heaton, Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw, Mount, Santos, Dorgu, Lacey, Amad, Mbeumo; Subs: Heath, Mee, Amass, Armer, Dalot, Yoro, Fernandes, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Tielemans, Zirkzee.

    Paris St-Germain: Safonov, Pacho, Zabarnyi, Koukaba, Boly, Beraldo, Dro, Mayulu, Kvaratskhelia, Ayari, Mbaye; Subs: Marquinhos, Mendes, Lucea, Vitinha, Neves, El Nay, Idder, Drame, Bourdin, Ndjantou, Meite, Longoni, Chevalier.

    And here’s a famous match that took place there, giving a certain Sir Alex Ferguson his first European trophy.

    “Get a bit sharper, get better on the ball, go up a notch.”.

    “It’s not about today it’s about preparing. Some players have played 90 minutes, some have played three games, some have just come back. So it’s about keeping working on things we’ve been working on.”.

    In a recent development, “They’re similar to us, but have fewer senior players available . They’ve had a great time and great squad so whoever on the pitch it will be a test.”.

    A hugely talented player for a number of clubs, including United, who ever really lived up to his early promise.

    Here’s a goal to dine out on...

    Good to have you back, lads 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/3EgkXLqcQm.

    📃 Le onze de départ pour cette rencontre de préparation face à Manchester United. #PSGMUN pic.twitter.com/LodcDM1Yrm.

    I expect they’ll make an appearence at some point.

    Ready to face PSG in our latest pre-season test ✊.

    Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

    Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

    One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

    Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

    Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

    This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

    In a recent development, “I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager remarked. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

    “The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”.

    Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

    A Bruxelles non basta il vantaggio di Pio Esposito: agli azzurri sarebbe servito un pareggio per andare ai quarti.

    L’Italia perde 4-1 contro il Belgio nell’ultima partita del girone di Nations League e manca la qualificazione ai quarti di finale. Dopo il 3-1 sulla Francia, a Bruxelles sarebbe bastato un pareggio. Gli azzurri passano invece in vantaggio con Pio Esposito, prima di subire la rimonta dei Red Devils.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    Il successo nella gara precedente non basta dunque all’Italia per proseguire nella competizione.

    Ai microfoni della Rai, il commissario tecnico Roberto Mancini riconosce la superiorità degli avversari e spiega dove gli azzurri hanno sofferto: «Sono stati migliori. Abbiamo pagato troppo a livello fisico e l’uno contro uno, nonostante avessimo iniziato bene. Sono stati più bravi. Abbiamo iniziato a soffrire, quando la palla arrivava sugli esterni facevamo fatica a fare pressing. Abbiamo pagato la partita contro la Francia a livello fisico. Hanno meritato, non possiamo dire nulla».

    #27232. Jaylen Brown to miss 76ers game Wednesday vs. Magic due to 'hamstring strain'

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (328 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Jaylen Brown to miss 76ers game Wednesday vs. Magic due to 'hamstring strain'

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (328 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Philadelphia 76ers will take on the Orlando Magic on Wednesday night, but without star shooting guard Jaylen Brown.
    • Recent findings suggest that he is dealing with a hamstring strain and has already been ruled out for tomorrow night's game.
    • Sources indicate that the guard is in his first season with the 76ers after the infamous trade that sent him to Philadelphia from Boston.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Philadelphia 76ers will take on the Orlando Magic on Wednesday night, but without star shooting guard Jaylen Brown.

    Recent findings suggest that he is dealing with a hamstring strain and has already been ruled out for tomorrow night's game. Brown picked up the injury during Philadelphia's win over the Brooklyn Nets on Monday.

    Sources indicate that the guard is in his first season with the 76ers after the infamous trade that sent him to Philadelphia from Boston. Brown has played in 14 games so far this season and is averaging 22.6 points, 6.6 rebounds, and 3.6 assists.

    The Philadelphia guard had a slow start with his fresh team, scoring 19 points in his team debut. The 76ers have tried to find the best fit among Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, Brown, and free-agent signee LeBron James.

    Sources indicate that it finally seemed to be clicking for Brown ahead of the injury. He logged back-to-back games with 31 points, his season high. The guard finished Monday night's win with a double-double: 31 points and 13 rebounds. He shot just 47.4% from the field, but he made 10 of 11 attempts from the charity stripe as Philadelphia beat Brooklyn 135-123.

    Without Brown in the lineup, the 76ers will likely give more minutes to Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Jabari Walker.

    According to recent reports, wednesday's game against Orlando will be Brown's second missed game this season. He also missed Philly's first game of a back-to-back against the New York Knicks.

    In a recent development, brown was dealing with both a head and a hamstring injury coming out of Monday's win against Brooklyn. After the game, he mentioned that he may have to get imaging done on Tuesday. Brown has been diagnosed with a left hamstring strain, but it remains unclear whether it will keep him out beyond Wednesday's game.

    Philadelphia has the Magic, Milwaukee Bucks, Portland Trail Blazers, Miami Heat, and Indiana Pacers in its next five games.

    Industry News: Top Wall Street analysts prefer these 3 dividend stocks for stable income

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade.
    • Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a tech giant's ability to pay dividends consistently.
    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade. Given this backdrop, investors seeking steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.

    Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a tech giant's ability to pay dividends consistently.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    It has been revealed that integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is a dividend king. The firm has increased its dividend for 39 consecutive years. At a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share (annualized dividend of $7.12 per share), CVX offers a yield of 3.14%. Chevron will announce its third-quarter results on October 30.

    In an earnings preview note on U.S. oil majors, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Chevron with a price target of $241. The analyst is focused on the company's international growth prospects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa, and the Eastern Mediterranean.

    Specifically, Mehta highlighted management's commentary on solid execution in Venezuela, with gross production expected to more than double to nearly 600 kbd (kilo barrels per day) by 2031 via three joint ventures. He also noted a recent oil and gas condensate discovery in offshore Angola and is awaiting commercial updates on the West Qurna 2 and Nasiriyah projects in Iraq.

    Furthermore, Mehta expects CVX to report improved productivity and capital efficiency across domestic shale assets. He expects the improvement mainly in the Permian Basin, where Chevron projects advanced chemical treatments to drive about a 10% recovery uplift in latest wells and bring down capital spend per barrel by about 25% year-over-year. Overall, Mehta expects Chevron to report Q3 2026 EPS of $4.95, above the consensus of $4.89.

    In a recent development, "While unfavorable timing effects and volatile commodity prices may present quarterly earnings headwinds, we highlight healthy U.S. refining margins and strong asset utilization as partial offsets," mentioned Mehta.

    Mehta ranks No. 381 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Chevron KPIs on TipRanks.

    Sources indicate that kinetik Holdings (KNTK) is a fully integrated, pure-play, midstream tech giant operating in the Delaware Basin. Earlier this month, the company declared a dividend of $0.81 per share, payable on October 30, 2026. With an annualized dividend of $3.24 per share, KNTK offers a yield of 5.82%. Kinetik will announce its Q3 earnings on November 4, with a conference call scheduled the next day.

    Ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, Goldman Sachs analyst John Mackay reiterated a buy rating on Kinetik stock and slightly raised his price target to $58 from $57. He expects the firm to report Q3 2026 EBITDA of $279 million, higher than the Street's expectation of $270 million but lower than the second quarter's EBITDA of $281 million.

    The 5-star analyst expects Kinetik's Q3 performance to gain from higher gas volumes after notable curtailments in the second quarter. Mackay also expects the quarter to benefit from higher production and steady commodity margins, even though some lower-margin contracts and weaker Waha spread marketing gains could weigh on results.

    Overall, Mackay increased his Q3 2026 estimates to reflect higher volumes, driven by rapid Permian egress pipeline commissioning, stronger throughput at Kings Landing I, and higher M2M commodity prices, offset by increased costs.

    "As natural gas takeaway constraints ease across the Permian, investor focus centers on KNTK's YE26 volume trajectory and durability of its multi-year growth," said Mackay.

    Mackay ranks No. 569 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.9%. See Kinetik's Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Moving to Crescent Energy (CRGY), an exploration and production tech giant with activities focused in the Eagle Ford, Permian, and Uinta Basins. With a quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share (annualized dividend of $0.48 per share), CRGY's dividend yield stands at 3.56%. Earlier this month, Crescent revealed an agreement to acquire Eagle Ford assets from Devon Energy (DVN).

    Recent findings suggest that heading into Q3 earnings on Nov. 2, Evercore analyst Stephen Richardson reiterated a buy rating on Crescent stock and slightly lowered the price target to $17 from $18, citing dilution from upcoming shares.

    "CRGY's recent acquisition of DVN's Eagle Ford assets marks a strategic, growth-oriented move, potentially enhancing cash flow performance," noted Richardson.

    In a recent development, the 5-star analyst noted that the acquisition of the Eagle Ford assets at a net purchase price of $3.85 billion will add about 68 MBoe/d of net production and over 600 net Tier 1 locations. Richardson added that a solid track record of synergies from past deals in the Eagle Ford region increases confidence about Crescent achieving efficiencies with this deal.

    Additionally, Richardson noted that the financial implications of the acquisition seem impressive, with a projected increase in cash flow per share of about 9% for 2027 to 2029.

    The analyst believes that Crescent is not just expanding its business through acquisitions but positioning itself as a more durable tech giant, regardless of market conditions.

    In a recent development, richardson ranks No. 478 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Crescent Energy Statistics on TipRanks.

    #27214. Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion

    📅 09 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 16m • 📚 Deep Dive (3124 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion

    📅 09 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3124 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.
    • The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.
    • Sources indicate that that goal also was supposed to set up penalties.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.

    The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.

    Sources indicate that that goal also was supposed to set up penalties. But after minutes of waiting around – and Kevin Campello, Chelsea’s head of first-team operations, saying “it’s written in the contract” – the players walked off the pitch.

    According to recent reports, that confusion ended a feisty affair in which tensions threatened to boil over and that, at certain points, paid little attention to the “friendly” aspect of the clash with seven yellow cards shown. At one point the visitors’ new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee exchanged angry words with some of Johor’s coaching staff. The CFC TV commentary team suggested that the spot-kicks were abandoned because of the match’s heated atmosphere.

    Austin MacPhee was ready to throw hands😂 pic.twitter.com/CFDgTOwmxE.

    Having played just 24 hours earlier in Jakarta – a 3-0 win over AC Milan – it was no surprise to see Xabi Alonso name a fresh XI, a mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters given much-needed game time.

    And considering Johor are one game away from setting a new world record of 109 matches unbeaten in the top flight – a run that would surpass the current mark set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s – it was also no shock to see the Malaysian team offer a stern, pre-season test for the west Londoners.

    In a recent development, after a good start Chelsea were second best in a first half in which Johor should have been at least two goals to the good. The Malaysian champions controlled the first 45 minutes and were 1-0 up after 14 minutes – a low cross from the left side-footed home by Arif Aiman.

    The hosts gave the young, inexperienced Chelsea backline a torrid time, especially on the flanks and Óscar Arribas was guilty of not capitalising on a great chance to double Johor’s lead, his shot after cutting in from the right going wide.

    Industry observers note that while they looked vulnerable at the back, Chelsea also struggled to keep possession in attack. But they got an equaliser they scarcely deserved after Liam Delap was manhandled to the ground in the box by Kevin Medina. The striker, who may well leave Stamford Bridge before the transfer window slams shut, fired home the spot-kick allowing the visitors to go into the break on level terms.

    For the most part, the second half followed a similar pattern to the first – Jofor having the better chances, while tensions on the pitch continued to run high.

    It was, however, Chelsea who took the lead after the break, Delap once again scoring from the spot, this time after Jamie Gittens was brought down in the area.

    Johor, though, kept on creating, thanks in part to a fairly porous visitors’ backline, and levelled through a deflected Arribas free kick, before going 3-2 up thanks thanks to a well-taken Bérgson strike.

    Sources indicate that had it stayed that way Chelsea could have had few complaints. But as the clock approached 90 minutes, the visitors had one last attack. Mykhailo Mudryk, just on as a substitute, delivered a cross from the left that Antonio Glauder could only steer into his own net. That was supposed to set up the penalty shoot-out that did not take place and the chance for one of the sides to claim a hollow victory.

    Sources indicate that considering a raft of changes and that fact this was far from the first XI, it is hard to know what to make of this. But among the positive things Alonso could take from the game was the impressive form of Nicolas Jackson and good centre-forward play of Delap. The negative was, however, a poor defensive display.

    Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge on Saturday for their last pre-season friendly, against Real Sociedad, before the Premier League season starts away at local rivals Fulham on August 24.

    Industry observers note that johor Darul Ta’zim: Syihan Hazmi; Arribas, Israfilov (Carlos Akapo 82), Medina, Antonio Glauder, Silva (La’Vere Corbin-Ong 89); Arif Aiman, Petrovic, Méndez (Nené 78), Marcos Guilherme (Bérgson); Zahedi (Stoichkov 62).     According to recent reports, there will NOT be a penalty shootout. No one is quite sure why.

    Anyway, that was an entertaining draw, plenty of good things for Chelsea (the play of Delap and Jackson) as well as worrying signs (open and vulnerable at the back).

    The commentators on CFC TV are now not so sure!

    It has been revealed that that was an entertaining pre-season friendly. There was a bit of niggle and that added to the action.

    There will be penalties, apparently, if it stays the same score...

    According to recent reports, will there be a late winner? There will be four minutes of added time.

    Mudryk just on picks up the ball on the left and, with four Chelsea players in the box, crosses into the danger area. It’s a good ball and asks too many questions of the hosts as Glauder diverts the ball into his own net.

    It’s been an entertaining match.

    It’s what the host have, on the balance of play, deserved, but it’s a gift from Chelsea. Essugo loses the ball in the final third and Bergson, on as sub pick it put driving at the box before hitting a low shot from outside the area, the ball nestling in the left corner of the net.

    Chelsea have been better this half than the first 45, they’ve been able to control the pace of the game well since the break.

    The pace has slowed down since the break, Chelsea seeing more of the ball. They work it right before Watson loses possession on the edge of the area.

    The referee clearly forgot about the hydration break and the two teams are having a belated one now. Delightful...

    I reckon there’s another goal left in this match. It’s been entertaining fare and the hosts have given as good as they’ve got, if not more.

    Recent findings suggest that this has been a lively match, better than most run-of-the-mill pre-season friendlies. Chelsea seeing a fair bit of possession at the moment, can they fashion a chance?

    Yes they can. But it’s a longish shot from Gittens that is easily saved by Hamzi in the JDT goal.

    According to recent reports, more niggle in this match that hasn’t really had many tough challenges. After a few handbags the referee takes control and the argy bargy peters out.

    It’s the least the hosts deserve. They have a free-kick 25 yards out, Arribas takes it with his right it’s at the wall but in turning away from the ball Delap deflects it into the far-right corner giving Slonina no chance.

    Fluky goal but the hosts have deserved their bit of luck.

    Delap again with the goal, this time he goes low, but still to the keeper’s right.

    Recent findings suggest that penalty for Chelsea. Gittens cuts back in the box onto his right and is clipped by the defender. Clear-cut penalty.

    In a recent development, half-chance for Delap on the edge of the area. He playes a one-two with Jackson before opening up his body and letting fly, the shot going well wide.

    Sources indicate that another good chance for the hosts and it’s not shock to write that it’s come from the industry of Arribas on the right. He fires in a low cross that evades everyone in the box.

    In a recent development, estevao goes down in the box, it looks as though it could well be a penalty but the referee waves play on. The Brazilian is the shown a yellow card for possibly lashing out having not got the decision he wanted.

    The hosts have asserted themselves well this half, in much the same way as they did in the first 45 minutes.

    Sources indicate that another good chance for the hosts and again it’s all too easy as Zahedi is one-on-one with the keeper. The striker, however, dithers a bit too long and Slonina makes a fine save. JDT have had plenty of chances to add to their sole goal...

    Chelsea have had a ragged start to this half.

    Good work from JDT who keep the ball well in midfield before a throughball is played to the on-rushing Zahedi but Slonina comes out well.

    They’re back under way in Johor, and there’s an early chance for Jackson who gets the ball in the box, but the ball gets stuck underneath him and he cannot get in a good attempt in on goal.

    And that is the last action of an entertaining half. Chelsea started well before the hosts opened the scoring. JDT then took control of the half and should, if truth be told, have extended their lead. But Delap did well to earn the penalty that he subsequently scored and should have made it 2-1 with the last kick of the 45.

    Worrying signs at the back, however, for Alonso. Will Chelsea go to four at the back after the break?

    The answer to that question (see last post) was so very nearly yes...

    Sources indicate that jackson plays in a peach of a through ball with the outside of his right foot, Delap is one-on-one with the keeper and looks for all the world as though he has to score. BUT he scuffs his shot wide.

    Industry observers note that there will be three minutes of added time. Can Chelsea head into the break with an unexpected lead?

    According to recent reports, free-kick for Chelsea on the JDT byline. The ball is put deep into the box, it’s headed back by Tosin before the ball is blazed over the bar.

    A minute later Tosin then let’s fly form 25 yards, the ball goes well over the bar.

    The hosts should have been more than 1-0 to the good and now they’re drawing. Goals change matches...

    Having won the penalty Delap fires the spotkick home, sending the keeper the the wrong way.

    Penalty to Chelsea and it’s all thanks to good centre-forward play by Delap. He gets the ball in the box and Medina manhands him to the ground. The referee doesn’t hesitate before pointing to the spot.

    In a recent development, chelsea have struggled to create anything since the opening 15 minutes. They have no control at the front and none at the back currently.

    As I type that JDT have another good chance to turn the 1-0 lead into a 2-0 lead. Arribas, whose been a menace all game, dances toward the Chelsea box before delaying the pass too long.

    Sources indicate that JDT are finding a lot of joy on the flanks, there are three at the back for Chelsea and on the outside are two youngsters. The hosts are working the space well.

    Sources indicate that yet again Chelsea are made to look decidedly average. A simple ball over the top on the right opens up the visitors’ defence and Arribas is in on goal, he cuts in and lets fly with his left peg, the shot going wide.

    That should have been 2-0 to the Malaysian powerhouses.

    Worrying signs for Chelsea who have struggled to keep possession up top and looked vulnerable at the back.

    Yet more good work from JDT who are being given space by Chelsea. Marcos Guilherme slaloms into the west Londoners’ box and Tosin again doesn’t look the most assured but the JDT player cuts the ball back and the visitors can clear the danger.

    Another good attack from the hosts who get in a shot in on goal, it’s deflected and loops into the grateful arms of Sharman-Lowe in the Chelsea goal.

    Sources indicate that there’s a break in play with Anselmino down and suffering what looks like a hamstring injury. He is eventually replaced by Reggie Watson.

    Meanwhile, the home fans are in fine voice and waving several HUGE flags.

    Yep, everyone’s least favourite part of the World Cup in the U, S of A is back. To be fair it’s humid in Johor so taking on fluids during the first 45 minutes is no bad idea.

    In a recent development, there’s a bit of argy-bargy not really what you should get in a ‘friendly’. There hasn’t been a bad chellenge in the match so far so not sure where that came from...

    Yet more good work from the hosts, this time it’s down the right, Arribas getting the better of Anselmino before shooting at the near post - the attempt hitting the side netting.

    After a lively start Chelsea have been second best.

    Poor defending from the visitors there but the chance was well snapped up by JDT.

    Lovely break from the hosts. They break down the left at pace, before the ball is threaded through to the back post and Arif Aiman sidefoots into the back of the net with aplomb.

    According to recent reports, so very nearly an opener for Chelsea. They break at pace thanks to Estevao who drives down the middle before playing in Jackson. The striker cuts in from the left and shoots, the attempt is saved well by Hamzi and Estevao’s follow up is wide. Is a goal coming?

    According to recent reports, free-kick for Chelsea some 35 yards out. Too far fro a shot on goal? Of course it is. The ball is floated into the box and the visitors earn a corner.

    Industry observers note that what can they create from this set piece? ‘Not much’ is the initial answer as the ball is cleared by JDT but Chelsea win possession back and the ball is fed to Estevao on the left, the Brazilian goes for go with his trusty left peg but the bal goes high and wide.

    JDT attack down the left, it’s a lovely ball in that forces a fine header to clear the danger from Adarabioyo.

    Recent findings suggest that no sooner had I sent that last post than Chelsea break through the middle. The ball is fed through to Delap who gets a left-footed shot in on goal forcing a good save from the JDT keeper Hamzi.

    Quiet, low-key start to the match. No real shock there, it is a pre-season friendly.

    Industry observers note that JDT give the ball away in their half and Chelsea have a half-decent platform to launch an attack from. They cannot fashion a chance and also lose possession.

    Sources indicate that they’re under way in southern Malaysia, Chelsea are in their vibrant blue and the hosts are wearing a fetching pink number. There was a late change for the visitors, Mamadou Sarr has been replaced by Olutayo Subuloye.

    We’re moments away from kick-off.

    According to recent reports, arriving for duty! 🫡 pic.twitter.com/M2XEkLC18n.

    Your Chelsea side today! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0OvvGVmgpc.

    A mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters you may not have heard of.

    Johor Darul Ta’Zim – more commonly known as JDT – are the Man Utd of Malaysia (at least that’s according to a Malaysian friend of mine). In 2013, they were going nowhere and were the dictionary definition of a stagnant club, low on confidence and trophies. That was until the Crown Prince bought the club and, over the next 13 years, transformed it into the powerhouse it is today.

    In a recent development, as if to underline JDT’s dominance over Malaysian football they are one game away from the world record unbeaten run in a top flight. The new season of the Malaysian Super League gets under way later this month and should they avoid defeat in their opening match they will extend their unbeaten run - which began in April 2021 - to 109 games and surpass the world record set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s.

    According to recent reports, chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

    A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

    The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

    Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

    Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

    Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

    “The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

    “We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our proposal and we’ve stuck to that.

    Recent findings suggest that “We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”.
